This is an exclamation made in response to a statement which the speaker thinks is foolish or stupid. (The exclamation {Dap!:sen:nolink} using the non-slang word {Dap:n} is also possible, though less likely.) If the speaker is referring to something that's happened which is a stupid thing to have happened (but really did happen, so that it's not a nonsensical statement), {chatlh:sen:nolink} or {Dap:sen:nolink} would not be used. Instead, a version of the idiomatic expressions {ghaH vuv SuS neH:sen} or {Dogh; tIghla' rur:sen@@Dogh:v, tIghla':n, rur:v} might be heard: ▶ {vuvpu' SuS neH vay'!:sen:nolink} "That's stupid!", "someone wanted the wind to respect him/her" ▶ {vogh tIghla' tu'lu':sen:nolink} "there's a t'gla somewhere" ▶ {HIv tIghla'!:sen:nolink} "a/the t'gla attacks"

This word is used for a broader range of objects than the translation "permit" suggests. Kinds of {chaw':n:nolink} include {HIjmeH chaw':n}, {Huch chaw':n}, {leng chaw':n}, {lojmIt chaw':n:nolink}, {yer ghajwI' chaw':n}, and {'elmeH chaw':n}. Thus, {chaw':n:nolink} can also mean "ticket", "pass", or "license". A {chaw':n:nolink} shows that you are officially or legally allowed to do or get or own something, whereas a {Qoyje':n} serves as proof or verification of some sort of achievement or accomplishment.[3]

While both {DaHjaj:n:nolink} and {jajvam:n} mean "today", they are not quite interchangeable. {DaHjaj:n:nolink} (but not {jajvam:n:nolink}) is used as the time element in a sentence: {DaHjaj romuluSngan vIHoHpu':sen:nolink} "today I killed a Romulan".[2] As the subject of a sentence, {jajvam:n:nolink} is more typically found, though {DaHjaj:n:nolink} is not impossible. Compare: ▶ {nI' jajvam:sen:nolink} "this day is long" ▶ {nI' DaHjaj:sen:nolink} "today is long"[2] {DaHjaj:n:nolink} also behaves as a noun in such noun-noun constructions as {DaHjaj gheD:n} "today's prey", a term often heard in Klingon restaurants with a meaning comparable to "catch of the day".[2] {DaHjaj:n:nolink} is also used with words indicating a time of day to refer to that portion of the current day. For example, {DaHjaj ram:n}, literally "today's night", means "tonight".[2] Other portions of the day, such as {pem:n}, {po:n:1h}, {pov:n}, and so on, are also possible. These can be shortened to {DaHram:n}, {DaHpem:n}, {DaHpo:n}, {DaHpov:n}, and so on.[3] As a time element, {DaHjaj:n} precedes any adverbials.[1, sec. 6.7]

definition: dish in a restaurant, "catch of the day"
definition_fr: plat dans un restaurant, "prise du jour"

notes: This is short for {DaHjaj pem:n@@DaHjaj:n, pem:n}.[1]
This is short for {DaHjaj po:n@@DaHjaj:n, po:n:1h}.[1]
This is short for {DaHjaj pov:n@@DaHjaj:n, pov:n}.[1]
This is short for {DaHjaj ram:n}.[1]

definition: May you die before you are captured.
regard as, view as, consider (treat somebody like)
definition_fr: considérer comme, voir comme, traiter comme

definition: type of animal, hippopotamus (hippo-like Klingon animal)
definition_fr: type d'animal, hippopotame (animal Klingon ressemblant à un hippopotame)
notes: This is the closest Klingon equivalent to a hippo.[1]
This refers to a device worn over the ears with both ears covered, with a band across the head, so that only the user can listen to something. The device Uhura wears is a {teS HablI':n}.
This means to make (an image) less blurry.[1]

This refers to a bunch or collection of threads, grass, hair, etc., held or growing together at the base.[1] This is any collection of filament-like things, not restricted to living material. The brush part of a paintbrush is a {Daqba':n:nolink}.[2]

This normally refers to a water well, but could be for other substances. It refers to a well which is constructed (or dug), rather than naturally occurring. If clarity is needed, one can say {bIQ Daqrab:n@@bIQ:n, Daqrab:n}.
There is an idiom, {jej; Daqtagh rur}.

This refers to a person with an "icy" demeanor, especially a tough negotiator. It is not clear whether this is a native Klingon word or a borrowed Trill or Kriosian word or phrase meaning "ice man," but, in any case, this is the Klingon pronunciation.[1]
This is not the same as a {velqa':n}, as a clone is not a replica (copy, model, etc.). It's the same thing as the original, and is genetically identical to it.[1]
This refers to the beverage only. For the dried-up mixture used to brew tea, see {Qenvob:n}.
In {TNK:src}, "cup and saucer" is translated as {Dargh HIvje' jengva' je:n@@Dargh HIvje':n, jengva':n, je:conj}.
This word is never followed by the locative suffix {-Daq:n:suff}. ({TKD 3.3.5:src})

This applies to movement by the whole body or thing to the left or right. It's not used if a person's feet stay put but the body leans left or right, for which see {ler:v}. This verb can be applied to aircraft, for which see {Dav:v:2}.[1]

definition: sway (aircraft moves to the side without yawing)
definition_fr: embarder (l'avion se déplace sur le côté sans lacet)
notes: This is just the verb {Dav:v:1} applied to aircraft.
This word covers the same semantic ground as the verbs {HoQ:v} and {Qaq:v} (but not really {mIl:v}).
This is what the wind does, so the subject is usually {SuS:n}.[1]
Watch the "A Klingon Christmas Carol" trailer where this is used: {YouTube video:url:http://youtu.be/5Nc5t9AZYsM}
The object is always plural, frequently in the form {A B je:sen:nolink}. If the comparison is being made between two (or more) of the same thing, the noun's plural suffix is generally not used.[1]
This refers to the viscous, sweet fluid produced from plant nectar.[1]
This is an ingredient in {ro'qegh'Iwchab:n}, which will turn out badly if the plant is overcooked.[2]
This refers to vehicular traffic. For a "traffic jam", the term {Hutvagh:n:nolink} is used.[1]
This is the second highest rank of {QaS:n:1h}.
This is a title for a warrior who has attained legendary status in life.
source: [1] {DS9 - Blood Oath:src}, [2] {A Good Day to Die:src}, [3] {Saarbrücken qepHom'a' 2014:src}

definition: a bird characterized by erratic, unpredictable behavior
definition_fr: un oiseau caractérisé par un comportement erratique et imprévisible
notes: This bird is similar to a {Da'vI':n}.

definition: a bird characterized by erratic, unpredictable behavior
definition_fr: un oiseau caractérisé par un comportement erratique et imprévisible
notes: This is similar to a {Da'nal:n}.
The object is the thing being surrounded. {-Daq:n:suff} is unnecessary.[2]
This can also refer to the suits in a deck of playing cards, for which see {meyrI':n}, {por:n}, {Sor:n}, and {'eSpeD:n}.
This refers to a duty station on a ship, not to something worn on the head (which would be {mIv:n:1}).
This expression may be based on {DeghwI':n}. In non-slang vocabulary, this idea can be expressed using a phrase such as {nab Hutlh 'ach vang:sen@@nab:n, Hutlh:v, 'ach:conj, vang:v}.[1, p.149]
There seems to have been a verb {Degh:v:hyp,nolink} at one time with the meaning of "steer" which has fallen out of use.[2]

definition_fr: être mûr, être trop mûr (fruit, légume)
notes: For Klingons, this is preferred to {baQ:v:2}.

definition: Your face looks like a collapsed star!
definition_fr: Ton visage ressemble à une étoile effondrée !

notes: This is a {no' Hol:n} expression used by a captain upon taking command of a ship.
This is the 83rd element of the periodic table.
This is the chemical element with the symbol Mo and atomic number 42.

definition: be clear, be transparent, be colourless
definition_fr: être clair, être transparent, être incolore
notes: Something which gradually vanishes (in terms of becoming less and less visible) may be said to {DemchoH:v@@Dem:v, -choH:v}. (Note that gradually does not necessarily mean slowly.) This might describe what people see when they are watching someone beaming away with a transporter beam. Once that person is gone, might use {ngab:v} to describe them. Using {loj:v} would be appropriate if one is focusing on the incremental disappearance of the person.[2]
This is also called {DenIbya':n:nolink}, typically by older speakers.[2]
This creature is also called {DenIbya' Qatlh:n:nolink}. Watch Gowron say this: {YouTube video:url:http://youtu.be/7qXuTn9HpP4}
A Denebian is also called a {DenIbya'ngan:n:nolink}.
She is a member of the House of D'Ghor ({Daghor tuq:n:name}).
source: [1] {DSC - Battle at the Binary Stars:src}, [2] {Saarbrücken qepHom'a' 2019:src}

notes: The suffix for the plural of this word depends on whether it is used to refer to beings capable of using language (see {-pu':n:suff}) or beings incapable of using language (see {-mey:n:suff}).
This verb is also used idiomatically, so that for example {Deq SuvwI'@@Deq:v, SuvwI':n} is similar to the English expression "That warrior is history".

definition: veer (to the left or right while traveling or moving)
definition_fr: virer (vers la gauche ou la droite en voyageant ou en se déplaçant)
notes: This means to change direction to the left or right while traveling or moving. This verb can be applied to aircraft, for which see {Der:v:2}.[1]

definition: yaw (aircraft nose points left or right)
definition_fr: dévier (le nez de l'avion pointe vers la gauche ou la droite)
notes: This is just the verb {Der:v:1} applied to aircraft.

definition: surrender (something), relinquish, give away, let go of
definition_fr: abandonner (quelque chose), abandonner, donner, lâcher prise

notes: This word is used for both the body part and the handle of a {nevDagh:n}. Note that the suffix {-Du':n} is used even with the latter meaning.
This refers to the inner part of the forearm, which extends from the palm to the elbow pit ({DeS tutren:n}).[1]
This refers to the entire upper part of the arm. Unless specificity is called for, {DeS:n:nolink} is generally left out of {DeS nev'ob:n:nolink}.[2]

This refers to the outer part of the forearm, which extends from the back of the hand to the outer part of the elbow. The other side is the {DeS Do'ghI':n}, while the entire forearm is the {cha'neH:n}. Unless specificity is called for, {DeS:n:nolink} is generally left out of {DeS reStav:n:nolink}.[2]

definition: cathetus, shorter side of right-angled triangle
notes: The three sides of a right-triangle ({ra'Duch leD:n}), relative to a non-right angle, are the {DeS Sum:n}, {DeS Hop:n}, and the {qubbID:n:2}.[1]

definition: opposite side (of an angle in a right triangle)
definition_fr: côté opposé (d'un angle dans un triangle rectangle)

definition: adjacent side (of an angle in a right triangle)
definition_fr: côté adjacent (d'un angle dans un triangle rectangle)

definition: pedal (foot lever such as for piano)
definition_fr: pédale (levier au pied comme pour le piano)
notes: This is a lever (with the fulcrum at one end) controlled by the foot, such as a pedal on a piano or organ. This is typically the object of the verb {ghujmoH:v@@ghuj:v, -moH:v}.[1]

This is a pedal with the fulcrum in the middle (rather than at one end) that is typically pressed downward with either the front of the foot or the heel. The verb {ghujmoH:v@@ghuj:v, -moH:v} is used with this.[1]

definition: closet, cupboard, cabinet, fixed storage device
definition_fr: placard, penderie, armoire, dispositif de rangement fixe
notes: This does not necessarily have to be fixed in place.
This is not a Klingon device as Klingons prefer live food, but refers to something found in many Terran homes.
This is the general term for being electrically charged (as opposed to being positively or negatively charged).[1]

definition: Knowledge of useful information may be unfortunate.
definition_fr: La connaissance d’informations utiles peut s’avérer malheureuse.

notes: This is a shortened form of {'ej De' vIchel:adv}. Klingon grammarians argue about whether the resulting {De'chel:adv} should be considered an adverbial in its own right.[1]

There is a single word for both stalactite and stalagmite. If a distinction is needed, one says {pa' beb De'lor:n@@pa' beb:n, De'lor:n} and {rav De'lor:n@@rav:n:1, De'lor:n}. One never says {rav'eq De'lor:n@@rav'eq:n, De'lor:n}.
A mechanical device that supports another part and/or reduces friction.[1]
This term is normally used only for fairly big (or powerful) computers.[2]
This is a component of a cloaking device. Note that it refers to a physical object and not a force field.
{maH:n:1h}:{chaH:n}/{bIH:n} = {DI-:v:pref,nolink}

This suffix turns a cardinal number into an ordinal number. For example, {wa'DIch:n:num} "first" from {wa':n:num} "one", {cha'DIch:n:1,num} "second" from {cha':n:num} "two", and so on. Ordinal numbers follow the noun to which they apply.
The locution {DIDmoH:v@@DID:v, -moH:v} is used to mean "speak of or refer to (whatever the object of the verb is) in stereotypical terms".[1]
Its leaf ({DIghna' por:n:nolink}) is fried (see {mIQ:v}) by experienced cooks.[1, p.94]
This is deep-fried (see {mIQ:v}) and eaten.[1, p.94]

definition: slide sword blade along opponent's blade
definition_fr: faire glisser la lame de l'épée le long de la lame de l'adversaire

definition: use a pigment stick, paint with pigment stick
definition_fr: utilisez un bâton de pigment, peignez avec un bâton de pigment
notes: The object of this verb is the thing which is touched by a {rItlh naQ:n}, for example a {nagh beQ:n}. Since {DIj:v:2,nolink} is already associated with {nagh beQ:n:nolink}, it can be left out. However, if painting or drawing on something other than a {nagh beQ:n:nolink}, it should be specified.[2] To specify the thing to be drawn, one can use the verbs {cha':v} or {nargh:v:0}. The latter means both "appear" and "escape", and similar to how {qon:v} is used for composing music or writing stories, its use suggests that the picture already exists and the {DIjwI':n} is somehow enabling it to escape and appear. Usually {nargh:v:0,nolink} is used with the suffix {-moH:v}, but it's also possible to use it without, though this construction is heard less frequently. The {cha':v:nolink} version is more common in informal settings and the {nargh:v:nolink} (usually {narghmoH:v:nolink}) version is more common in literature or in discussions about art.[2] This verb can be used for producing a visual image even if no paint or pigment stick is involved, for example with a pencil, or with a device or computer software.[2]
This is one of three key ingredients neede to make {ngat:n:1}.
This is a traded commodity, like {qevaS:n}.

definition: open entryway (to corridor, tunnel, conduit, Jeffries tube, branch of sewer)
definition_fr: entrée ouverte (vers couloir, tunnel, conduit, tube Jeffries, branchement d'égout)
notes: This refers to the open entryway leading into a longish enclosed space, or in other words a {qa'rI':n} at or from which one can enter or exit. If there's a door there, the door is referred to by the usual word, {lojmIt:n}.[2; 3]
source: [1] {HQ 12.2, Jun. 2003:src}, [2] {KLI mailing list 2019.04.11:src}, [3] {Saarbrücken qepHom'a' 2019:src}, [4] {message to KLI Discord 2024.11.27:src}

notes: This is generally used for things spinning or rotating continuously or for a long time, while {jIr:v} is used when the thing rotates partially or once or for a few times. For example, one would {jIrmoH:v:2} the steering wheel of a car, while the tires {DIng:v:nolink}.[2]
This is a slang term for the device and the most common way to refer to it.[1]

Noun Type 1: Augmentative/diminutive ▶ {-'a':n:suff} ▶ {-Hom:n:suff} ▶ {-oy:n:suff} Noun Type 2: Number ▶ {-pu':n:suff} ▶ {-Du':n:suff} ▶ {-mey:n:suff} Noun Type 3: Qualification ▶ {-qoq:n:suff} ▶ {-Hey:n:suff} ▶ {-na':n:suff} Noun Type 4: Possession/specification ▶ {-wIj:n:suff} / {-wI':n:suff} ▶ {-lIj:n:suff} / {-lI':n:suff} ▶ {-Daj:n:suff} ▶ {-maj:n:suff} / {-ma':n:suff} ▶ {-raj:n:suff} / {-ra':n:suff} ▶ {-chaj:n:suff} ▶ {-vam:n:suff} ▶ {-vetlh:n:suff} Noun Type 5: Syntactic markers ▶ {-Daq:n:suff} ▶ {-vo':n:suff} ▶ {-mo':n:suff} ▶ {-vaD:n:suff} ▶ {-'e':n:suff}

This word takes the suffix {-Du':n:suff} when it refers to skin still on the body, and {-mey:n:suff} otherwise.[2] (But see {nagh DIr:n} for how to form the plural when it is used to refer to an animal shell.)
When the context is clear, this is sometimes shortened to {DIr bID:n}.
This is the name of a specific skin disease from the time of Kahless.
This can refer to one pattern/design, or to a whole lot of them taken together.
This is a drum made with animal skin stretched over a cylinder, usually over only one end. If skin is stretched over both ends of a drum, it is an {'o'lav:n}.[1]
This is a type of {SuSDeq:n}.
For "years ago" and "years from now", see {ben:n:1} and {nem:n}, respectively. For "years old", see {ben:n:2}.

There is no traditional Klingon way to say "Happy New Year", though a Klingon might understand {DIS chu' yItIv@@DIS:n:2, chu':v:1, yI-:v, tIv:v} or {DIS chu' DatIvjaj@@DIS:n:2, chu':v:1, Da-:v, tIv:v, -jaj:v} or {DIS chu' botIvjaj@@DIS:n:2, chu':v:1, bo-:v, tIv:v, -jaj:v}.[1]

This is a day on which one recognizes or remembers an event which occurred a number of years ago. Other units of time are possible, such as {jarjaj:n} and {Hoghjaj:n}. It's also possible to use other units of time such as {tupjaj:n@@tup:n, jaj:n} as a form of word play. Both cardinal numbers ({DISjaj wa':n@@DISjaj:n, wa':n:num}) and ordinal numbers ({DISjaj wa'DIch:n@@DISjaj:n, wa'DIch:n}) are acceptable for referring to anniversaries.

This can refer to any path or route with the same starting and ending point. The path doesn't have to be circular, though it often is. Thus it can be used for "orbit" or "lap (around a track)", for example.[1]
This is the name of a Federation starship.
This is the Klingon plant most like a fern. For the Earth plant, precede with {tera':n}.[1]

This word is used to refer to "the Federation", a shortened form of "the United Federation of Planets" ({yuQjIjDIvI':n}). Coincidentally or not, this words sounds similar to {DI vI':n:nolink} "it accumulates debris".

definition_fr: Parlez-vous le standard de la Fédération ?
Croiseur de combat de la Fédération
être coincé (physiquement, il ne bougera pas)
notes: This means something is stuck like when you can't get a door or window open.
This means to review something for the purpose of making or suggesting changes.[1]
This can be used for "personality" in the sense of a quality or trait that forms a person's character.[2]

definition: type of animal, sheep (fluffy, woolly, shaggy Klingon animal)
definition_fr: type d'animal, mouton (animal Klingon pelucheux, laineux, hirsute)
notes: This is a fluffy, woolly, shaggy Klingon animal. A ram would be a {DI'raq loD:n@@DI'raq:n, loD:n}, and an ewe would be a {DI'raq be':n@@DI'raq:n, be':n}.
Contrary to the general pattern with {QeD:n}, this is written as two words. A person who does this is a {DI'ruj tej:n@@DI'ruj:n, tej:n}.[2]
This is a {Qe':n} with a sign that says {moD Soj:sen@@moD:v, Soj:n:1}.[1, p.102]

definition: be cruel, be merciless, be brutal
definition_fr: être cruel, être impitoyable, être brutal

definition: be polite, be civil, be courteous
definition_fr: être poli, être courtois, être civil
notes: This describes a rather un-Klingon way to behave.

definition: How much do you want for that?

definition_fr: Je ne peux pas manger ça.
Je ne peux pas boire ça.

notes: This refers to the separator used in specifying a set of coordinates, and not to a specific coordinate point or location (for which see {Quv:n}).
There is an idiom {Dogh; tIghla' rur:sen@@Dogh:v, tIghla':n, rur:v}.[2, p.127]

definition: back away from, back off, get away from

notes: See {qawmoH:v} for an example of how to use a verb like this one.
This word can refer to people or otherwise. Even if referring only to beings capable of using language, one would normally say {Dojmey:n} rather than {Dojpu':n:nolink}.[1]

definition: mass, masses, multitude, a very large but indeterminate group of something
definition_fr: masse, masses, multitude, un groupe très vaste mais indéterminé de quelque chose
notes: This word can refer to people or otherwise. Even if referring only to beings capable of using language, one would normally say {Dojmey:n:nolink} rather than {Dojpu':n:nolink}.[1]
To say that two or more things are parallel, this verb is used with a plural subject.[2]

This refers to a direction like "left" and "right", and not to the side surface of an object which also has a front and a back, for which see {reD:n:3}.[4] In {Klingon Monopoly:src}, {Dop:n:nolink} is used to indicate one face of a playing card.[3]

definition: be opposite, be antithetical, be contradictory
definition_fr: être opposé, être antithétique, être contradictoire
notes: The construction {DopmoH:v} is used for reversing a list.[1] This is also used as a single-word sentence (without affixes) meaning something like "on the contrary" or "au contraire". A stronger version is the idiomatic {bIQ ngaS HIvje'lIj.:sen@@bIQ ngaS HIvje'.:sen}[2]
This is just the verb {Dop:v:1} applied to numbers in mathematics.

definition: Set fire on the side when there is danger.
definition_fr: Allumez le feu sur le côté en cas de danger.

notes: This verb also covers colors which would be called "brown". To differentiate a brown object from another object which could also be described using {Doq:v:nolink}, a phrase such as {Doq 'ej wovbe':sen@@Doq:v, 'ej:conj, wov:v, -be':v} is used.[2] The word {Doqqu':v@@Doq:v, -qu':v} refers to a color more red than orange.[3]

The expressions {Doq bIQtIq:sen:nolink} ("the river is red") and {Doq bIQtIq bIQ:sen:nolink} ("the river water is red") can be traced back to an old drinking song commemorating the slaying of {molor:n:name} by {qeylIS'e' lIjlaHbe'bogh vay':n:name}.

definition: to be a particular shade of brown
definition_fr: être d'une nuance particulière de brun
notes: A kradge has brown lips. This expression is used to describe an object which is a particular shade of brown (see {Doq 'ej wovbe':sen}).
To be more specific about the shade of brown, a comparison is used. For example, one might say {Doq 'ej Qaj wuS rur:sen} (kradge lips are a particular shade of brown).[1]
The object of this verb can be physical things such as a territory or a sword, or more abstract concepts such as authority.

definition: sink for cleaning hands, face, food, etc.
definition_fr: évier pour nettoyer les mains, le visage, la nourriture, etc.
notes: A bathtub or swimming pool would be a {DoQmIv'a':n}. A {DoQmIvHom:n@@DoQmIv:n, -Hom:n} would be a bucket or anything similar.
If necessary, "bathtub" and "swimming pool" can be distinguished using qualifiers: {Say'moHmeH DoQmIv'a':n}, {QalmeH DoQmIv'a':n}.

definition_fr: finir, se terminer (une période de temps)
notes: The subject of this verb is a period or unit of time, such as a month. It should not be an event the ending of which one has some control over (for which see {van:v:2}, {ghang:v}).
This idiomatic expression, which literally means to lose or misplace a target, means "to digress". {DoS vIchIl:sen:nolink} means "I digress", and so on.
This is generally crafted from bone.
This can be used with people, but has a disparaging connotation, unlike {choy:v} which is used only with people.[1]

definition_fr: chariot (véhicule à roues, tiré ou poussé)
notes: This can have any number of wheels (typically two).

definition_fr: avoir de la chance, être chanceux

notes: This is essentially the verb {Do'Ha':v} as a standalone sentence.

Though originally referring to a mass of creatures of some sort (such as {maqSung Do':n@@maqSung:n, Do':n:1} "swarm of bees"), the word's meaning is sometimes broadened and used for masses of inanimate objects (such as {wolmeye' Do':n@@wolmeye':n, Do':n:1} "swarm of drones"). {HoSDo':n:nolink} may have formerly been {HoS Do':n@@HoS:n:1, Do':n:1}.[1]

definition_fr: mollet (arrière du bas de la jambe)
notes: This means the back of the lower leg. It's possible to say {'uS Do'ghI':n:nolink}, but {'uS:n:nolink} tends to be used only if a distinction or comparison is being made with {DeS Do'ghI':n}.[2]
This is the name of a planet which was disputed between the United Federation of Planets ({yuQjIjDIvI':n}) and the Klingon Empire ({tlhIngan wo':n}).
This is the kind of stone Klingons use to sharpen their knives, bat'leths, and so on.[1]
{ghaH:n}/{'oH:n}:{SoH:n} = {Du-:v:pref,nolink}

The object is the thing which is improved. This verb is used for improvement of a more abstract nature, such as in status, skill, understanding, etc. For improvement in a more concrete sense, see {rach:v}.[2]

definition: If it's in your way, knock it down.
definition_fr: Si cela vous gêne, faites-le tomber.

notes: {nach Hom:n@@nach:n, Hom:n:1} is also fine, but {DughrI':n:nolink} is a more technical term.
This can be used for a "setting" in a {SeHlaw:n}.[2]
This is a type of {jem'IH:n}. This word can be used if the emphasis is to be on the elegance or grandeur of the building.

definition: type of animal, lobster (Klingon animal found in water with a huge claw)
definition_fr: type d'animal, homard (animal Klingon trouvé dans l'eau avec une énorme griffe)
notes: This is a Klingon animal found in the water which has a huge claw.[1]

search_tags: vehicle, craft, boat, barge, spaceship, starship
notes: This word can refer to any vehicle, not just spaceships, by specifying the environment in which the vehicle travels. See {puH Duj:n}, {muD Duj:n}, {bIQ Duj:n}. Some special terminology is used for the parts of a {Duj:n:1h,nolink}. The section towards its {tlhop:n:1h} is called its {'et:n:2h}, while the section towards its {'em:n} is called its {'o':n}. To refer to a ship's dorsal, ventral, port, and starboard areas, see {Dung:n}, {bIng:n}, {poS:n}, and {nIH:n}, respectively. For verbs related to ship movement, see under {'or:v}. This word has a negative connotation in Klingon culture.[1]

This refers to a specific video file.[2]

This is typically round (so it could be a {'Ib rutlh:n@@'Ib:n, rutlh:v}) and portable (so it's not a {qegh:n}).[1]

The act of issuing the challenge is {poQ:v}, which is short for {qab legh 'e' poQ:sen@@qab:n, legh:v, 'e':n, poQ:v} "He/she demands to see a face". Hitting one's adversary with the back of the hand ({chap:n}) while issuing the challenge is to demand a duel to the death ({Hay'chu':v}).[2] To agree to the duel, say {vISo'be':sen@@vI-:v, So':v:1, -be':v} "I don't hide it" (or the longer {qabwIj vISo'be'.:sen} "I don't hide my face"). The challenged party is then said to {'angchu':sen@@'ang:v, -chu':v} (short for {qab 'angchu':sen@@qab:n, 'ang:v, -chu':v}). One accepts a challenge ({qab 'ang:sen@@qab:n, 'ang:v}) in order to prove one's honor ({quv tob:sen@@quv:n, tob:v}).[2]
This is just the verb {Hay':v} with the suffix {-chu':v}. From the Klingon point of view, to duel perfectly is to duel to the death.[1]

The fact that {yIn:v} can be used transitively suggests that {Hegh:v:nolink} can be too.

definition_fr: La seule réussite d'un imbécile est la mort.

notes: This may also be written as {Heghba':n:nolink}.

definition_fr: Lorsqu'un guerrier meurt, son esprit s'échappe.
notes: The verb {nargh:v:2} means "escape", but it (or a phonetically identical word) also means "appear" (see {nargh:v:1}).

definition: Death is an experience best shared.
definition_fr: La mort est une expérience qu’il vaut mieux partager.

This is an admirable trait and does not carry connotations of arrogance, for which see {nguq:v}.

definition: Klingons are a proud race, and we intend to go on being proud.
definition_fr: Les klingons sont une race fière et nous avons l'intention de continuer à l'être.

In the {paq'batlh:n}, {molor:n:name} is referred to as a {HI''a':n:nolink} "tyrant" throughout.

notes: If {Hoch:n:nolink} is followed by a noun which is explicitly plural, it means "all the X's", taken collectively. definition_fr: Pitié pour le guerrier qui tue tous ses ennemis.
notes: This is a famous line from the poem {lu qeng:n:name,nolink} by G'trok. The idiomatic expression {Hoch jaghpu'Daj HoHpu':sen:nolink} "He/she has killed all his/her enemies" means that a person leads a meaningless, empty life, one lacking any challenge.
This idiomatic expression, which is based on the homophony of the words {nuH:n:1} and {nuH:n:2}, means "to consider every possibility" or "to consider every option".

This is the 5th rank of {yaS:n:1h}.[2] Watch Gowron say this: {YouTube video:url:http://youtu.be/9CTfqKn383I}

The Klingon week has six days, which are: ▶ {DaSjaj:n} "Monday" ▶ {povjaj:n} "Tuesday" ▶ {ghItlhjaj:n} "Wednesday" ▶ {loghjaj:n} "Thursday" ▶ {buqjaj:n} "Friday" ▶ {lojmItjaj:n} or {ghInjaj:n} "Saturday" If an alien calendar contains more than six days, additional days are numbered beginning with {wa':n:num}. The identifier is usually a country, region, or political unit of some kind. For example, Federation Standard (i.e., "English") is {DIvI' Hol:n}. {tlhIngan Hol:n:nolink} is actually a shortened form of {tlhIngan wo' Hol:n:nolink}.[2]

definition: be honored falsely, be falsely honorable
definition_fr: être faussement honoré, être faussement honorable
search_tags: be honoured falsely, be falsely honourable
notes: Deception is implied by the use of this verb. This word is used in places where {quv:v} might be used, but when the honor was discovered to be illegitimate. For example, a {Duy quv:n:nolink} who turns out to be a spy would be called a {Duy HoQ:n:nolink}. It differs from {quvHa':v} in that it indicates that one has demanded respect which is unearned or undeserved. A warrior who shows cowardice in battle is a {SuvwI' quvHa':n:nolink}. One who hides his cowardice, is awarded for valor (i.e., becomes known as a {SuvwI' quv:n:nolink}), and is subsequently discovered to be a fraud, is a {SuvwI' HoQ:n:nolink}. Do not use this word lightly as it has very bad connotations in Klingon society.
There is an idiom, {HoS; 'Iw rur:sen@@HoS:v, 'Iw:n, rur:v}. This verb is also used for regular polygons and polyhedra.[2]
This is a device which changes energy from one form to another.

notes: {pIraqSIS:n} is an important Klingon energy facility.
This refers to the magnitude of a wave (such as an electromagnetic wave). This literally means "strength" (see {HoS:n:1}).

The homophonous {Hotlh:v:1} suggests that this verb refers to the combined act of both capturing and displaying an image.
This refers to an astronomical body, and not to the geometric figure, for which see {DujtlhuQ:n}.

This literally means "money plate". It is often, but not always, followed by {-Hom:n}.

This means "strange" as in unfamiliar.[2]

This refers to identity.[1]
This is an application of {Hur:n:1} used in the sense of background music, instrumental background, background signal, and so on.[1]

To differentiate them, a submarine would be a {bIQ Hurgh Duj:n@@bIQ:n, Hurgh Duj:n} and a blimp would be a {muD Hurgh Duj:n@@muD:n:1, Hurgh Duj:n}.[1] A {Hurgh Duj:n:nolink} typically has a motor for propulsion.[2]
There is an idiom, {wIH; Hur'Iqngan rur@@wIH:v, Hur'Iqngan:n, rur:v}.

There are a few verbs whose meanings include locative notions. The objects of such verbs indicate the location, and the locative suffix {-Daq:n:suff} need not be used on them (but it is also not wrong to use it). If a noun which is not the object is marked with {-Daq:n:nolink}, it indicates the location where the action is taking place.[2] If the pronominal prefix is one which can indicate a direct object, and there is a noun marked with {-Daq:n:suff}, then either it is the direct object, or the direct object must be explicitly stated, even if it's a pronoun.[4]

The Klingon day goes from dawn to dawn. For the part of a day during which there is daylight, see {pem:n} (the opposite of which is night, {ram:n}). The parts of a {jaj:n:nolink} are: {pem:n} "daytime", {jajlo':n} "dawn", {po:n:1h} "morning", {pemjep:n} "midday", {DungluQ:n} "noon", {pov:n} "afternoon", {ram:n} "night", {ramjep:n:1} "midnight". For "days ago" and "days from now", see {Hu':n} and {leS:n}, respectively.
The Klingon week ({Hogh:n}) contains six days. Days beyond the sixth on alien calendars are simply numbered, starting at {wa':n:num}.[3]

A typical object of this verb is that which is spoken, which might be a language or lecture. The listener is the indirect object and is marked with {-vaD:n}.[3; 4] The "prefix trick" may be used with this verb: if the verb prefix indicates a first- or second-person object, that person is the indirect object, that is, the person to whom the subject is speaking.[3] The "prefix trick" also works for third-person indirect objects in situations where it is unambiguous.[7] The verb {jatlh:v:nolink} is also used when giving a direct quotation, in which case the verb prefix indicating no object is used (except if the "prefix trick" is applied). The quotation may come before or after the sentence with {jatlh:v:nolink}.[3] This is one of the few "verbs of speech" in Klingon. In Klingon, quotations must always be accompanied by one of these verbs.[4] For expressing "read aloud" (e.g., a book), something like {paq mu'mey jatlh:sen:nolink} would work.[6]

This is the general verb for measurement. The subject of this verb is taking the measurement of the object.[2] To indicate the length, width, and depth of an object, see {'aD:v}, {juch:v:1}, and {Saw':v}, respectively. For objects which are much longer or taller than they are wide, use {'ab:v:1} instead of {'aD:v}. The Klingon unit of linear measure is the {'uj:n}. Distances can be described using {chuq:n}, {Sum:v}, and {Hop:v}. For large distances, use {qelI'qam:n}; for even larger (e.g., interstellar) distances, use {loghqam:n}. To express an area, use {men:v}. See also {morgh:n} for a unit of area. To express a volume, use {muq:v} (see also {tIn:v}, {mach:v}). See {tlho'ren:n} for a unit of volume. To express a weight (mass), use {ngI':v} (see also {tIS:v}, {'ugh:v}). See {cheb:n} for a unit of weight or mass. To express a temperature, use {gheH:v}. See {SImyon:n} for a unit of temperature.
This refers to the sound, and not to any letter or glyph.
In other words, "upload" (or possibly "download", depending on context).

This is an insect found on {Qo'noS:n} which, like a cicada, can be rather noisy. To refer to the Terran insect, say {tera' labmIt:sen@@tera':n, labmIt:n} if clarity is needed. The {labmIt:n:nolink} is often informally referred to as {ghum ghew:n:nolink}, presumably because of what its "song" may resemble.[1]
This is sometimes preceded by {maqSung:n}.
This is the 8th rank of {yaS:n:1h}.[2]
This can also be used to express "feature" in the sense used in software.[2]
A patron at a {Qe':n} may {lajQo':v:nolink} a dish if the {jabwI':n} has {qawHa':v}.[1, p.102]
This is the kind of rake used for loosening the soil or smoothing the ground.[2]
This verb can be used with the suffix {-chu':v} to express the idea of superimposing something on(to) something else.[2] See {tIr:v}.

definition: row or line (of people or things expected to be in motion)
definition_fr: rangée ou ligne (de personnes ou de choses censées être en mouvement)
notes: This would be used for a queue, i.e., a line of people waiting to get into a movie. It is expected that the row or line of people or things is (or will or might be) in motion, so that eventually it diminishes until it's gone (in contrasted to a {wIyqap:n} which is stationary). This word is used even if the people or things are bunched up. If there are two rows of people waiting to get into two side-by-side entrances, {lanSoy:n:nolink} would still be used for each of them (and not {wev:n}).[1] The word {mIr:n:1} can be used as a slang term for this, if things are clear.[1]
This and {vaS:v} can be used both for the outer measurement of a thing, and also the inner measurement of an opening, for instance.[3]
This is to vote in an election or to vote for a motion. It doesn't have the idiomatic sense of "express an opinion" and is only used if a formal vote is actually taken.[1]

This verb describes movement like that of a bird's wings, and not like that of a flag (for which see {joq:v}). In flight, a bird's wings {laq:v:1:nolink}, and the bird is said to {laqmoH@@laq:v:1, -moH:v} its wings.
The non-slang way to say this would be {jat Hol jatlh:sen@@jat Hol:n, jatlh:v}.

definition_fr: tirer, mettre sous tension (par exemple, des propulseurs)

notes: The object of this verb is the odor being smelled.[2]
This is matter produced by an infected wound.[1]

definition: ink up, put paint on a brush
definition_fr: encre, mets de la peinture sur un pinceau
notes: This is used both for the act of transferring ink from a {rItlh 'echlet:n} to a {toqwIn:n}, and the act of putting paint on a {rItlh naQ:n}. A slang term for this action is {pID:v:2}.

The suffix for the plural of this word depends on whether it is used to refer to beings capable of language (see {-pu':n:suff}), body parts (see {-Du':n:suff}), or things which are neither (see {-mey:n:suff}).

definition: Pour the cold bloodwine into another glass!
definition_fr: Versez le vin de sang froid dans un autre verre !
notes: This idiomatic expression means "I don't believe you, maybe someone else will", or "That is irrelevant to me, maybe someone else will care."
Less formally, one could end the list of things by saying {latlh latlh latlh:sen@@latlh:n, latlh:n, latlh:n} or {taH taH taH:sen@@taH:v:1, taH:v:1, taH:v:1}.[1]

This means to move to a slanted or angled position. The starting position is often, but doesn't have to be, upright or perpendicular. If applied to a person, it means the person's feet stay put. The pivot could be at the top, bottom, or somewhere else. Returning to the upright (or earlier) position is {lavHa':v@@lav:v, -Ha':v}. If the swinging is continuously back and forth, use {ler:v} instead.
This is a traditional (in the sense of having been used a long time ago but no longer in use today) unit of angle. There are 243 {lawmey:n:nolink} in a {gho:n}. (Note that 243 is 3 to the 5th power.)

This is a modern unit of angle adopted from other civilizations in the galaxy. It is also referred to as a {law chu':n:nolink} (although that term is used less and less). There are 360 {lawrI'mey:n:nolink} in a {gho:n}.
The word {law':v:nolink} is used in comparative constructions. See {... X law' ... X puS:sen}. For things that are measurable or quantifiable, but not necessarily countable, use {vItlh:v}.[2]

search_tags: comparative, comparison, superlative, more, less, most, least
notes: This construction is used to form comparatives and superlatives. The two things being compared go into the two slots. To form the superlative, {Hoch:n} is used in the second slot.[1] Other antonym pairs may be substituted in place of {law':v} and {puS:v:1} as a form of word play, an example of intentional ungrammaticality. Such an advanced construction should be avoided unless one is very familiar with Klingon culture.[2] To say that something is not more {X:sen:nolink} than something else, {law'be':v:nolink} and {puSbe':v:nolink} are used instead of {law':v:nolink} and {puS:v:nolink}. To say that something is as {X:sen:nolink} as something else, {law':v:nolink} is used with {law':v:nolink} (if the quality or its possession is considered positive), or {puS:v:nolink} is used with {puS:v:nolink} (if the quality or its possession is considered negative), or {law':v:nolink} is used with {rap:v} or {nIb:v} (the latter of which implies the two things being compared are exactly the same in some way). It is also possible to use {puS:v:nolink} with {rap:v} or {nIb:v}, but that carries a connotation of disparagement. To say that something is not as {X:sen:nolink} as something else, {pIm:v} is used in place of the second verb in the pair.[3] To say that two things have the same amount of some quality, it's also possible to use {rap:v} or {nIb:v} without a {law':v:nolink}/{puS:v:nolink} construction. (See those verbs for details.) The above constructions are typically used only to compare similar things. To form similes, which compare things which are unlike, use {rur:v} instead. When the above constructions are used to compare unlike things, they generally reference well-known similes.

notes: This is some sort of technical term. It would be odd to say {lay vItlhuH:sen@@lay:n:2, vI-:v, tlhuH:v:1} for "I breathe air", but it would be understood.
A "wake" in this sense is a turbulent impression of a path left behind a vessel or object as it moves through fluid such as water or air.[1]
This refers to the coating or patina that develops on certain metals. If the color matters, {SuD:v:1} should be used.[1]
This is the 6th rank of {yaS:n:1h}.[2] Do not confuse this with {ra'wI':n}, which is also translated as "commander" in English, but has a different meaning.[2]
A planet in the Ferengi Alliance.
This refers to a whistling sound produced by using one's mouth and lips (and perhaps fingers, but no device).[1]
The {la'quv:n:nolink} is head of the Klingon High Command, and the highest ranked {yaS:n:1h}.[2]
This refers to a group of silicate minerals whose crystals can be easily split into thin elastic leaves.[1]
This refers to a Klingon creature that resembles a Terran turtle, which might be called a {tera' la'SIv:n:nolink}.
This is an officer in charge of certain specialized units within the military.

definition_fr: faire chanter, faire du chantage à
notes: The object of this verb is the victim of blackmail.

definition_fr: ligne de coordonnées (système de coordonnées traditionnel)

definition: be perpendicular, be at a right angle
definition_fr: être perpendiculaire, être à angle droit
notes: This is normally used with a plural subject.

definition: A sharp knife is nothing without a sharp eye.
definition_fr: Un couteau bien aiguisé n'est rien sans un œil aiguisé.

notes: For the removal of something from the exterior, consider {teq:v}.
The inhabitants of Lenmak use an eight-day week ({Hogh:n}).
This is a disease caused by a bacterium. Its symptoms include high fever, weakness, and perhaps abdominal pain, headaches, and a skin rash. Klingons tend to avoid talking about it.[1]
{leng:v:nolink} works like {jaH:v}.[2] This word can be used to refer to traveling with or without a special purpose. If it is desired to indicate traveling on a mission, use {ve':v} instead.[3]

definition_fr: système de contrôle de réaction de vol

notes: This may be applied to any meal, e.g., {leng megh:n:nolink} "voyage lunch" (see {megh:n}). See {KGT p.103:src} for a fuller explanation.
This can also refer to a button, such as on an {'eQway':n}.

This describes the back-and-forth motion of something fixed at one end to a pivot. When applied to a person, it means the feet stay put on the ground while the body leans left and right.[1] The pivot could be at the top, bottom, or somewhere else. A rhythmic oscillation like that of a pendulum would be {lerchu':v}.[2] For motion around a pivot in one direction only, which comes to a stop, see {lav:v}.[2] For movement to the side without rotation or being fixed to a point, see {Dav:v:1}.

This refers to the rhythmic back-and-forth motion of something fixed at one end, like a pendulum, whether the pivot is at the top, the bottom (like the inverted pendulum of a metronome), or somewhere else.
This is a type of {HurDagh:n}. It is larger than the {Supghew:n} but smaller than the {tIngDagh:n}.
For "be hard (be difficult)", see {Qatlh:v}. This word can be used figuratively. There is an idiom, {let mInDu'Daj; Separmey rur@@let:v, mIn:n, -Du':n, -Daj:n, Separ:n, -mey:n, rur:v}.
This is the metallic chemical element with the symbol Hg and atomic number 80.
The stairway leading to door of a ship is referred to by a more specific word, {choghvat:n:1}.

definition: stairway leading to door of a ship
definition_fr: escalier menant à la porte d'un vaisseau
notes: In some {meqro'vaq Sep:n} dialects, this refers to what is elsewhere called a {choghvat:n:1}.

definition: move bat'leth from vertical to horizontal orientation
definition_fr: passer bat'leth de la verticale à l'horizontale

notes: This is not used for monetary (or equivalent) compensation, for which see {teb:v:2}.[1]
This is actually a kind of Klingon nut, but it looks sort of like an almond. For the Terran almond, precede with {tera':n}.[1]
This is used for flowers, but can also be used for leaves.[1]
This is the 5th element of the periodic table.
The word for nose is {ghIch:n} everywhere, but in some regions this word is used as an alternative.[1, p.28]

definition_fr: ne pas être exceptionnel, ne pas être spécifique
notes: This can be used in the sense of "general" (as opposed to specific). For example, {nav HablI' le'be'} might refer to the general or shared fax machine at the front desk of an office, as opposed to a fax machine at someone's desk.[2]
This is anyone tasked with delivering a message. In some contexts, it (or sometimes {Qun le''aq:n@@Qun:n, le''aq:n}) may be translated as "angel".[1]
{ghaH:n}/{'oH:n}/{chaH:n}/{bIH:n}:{tlhIH:n} = {lI-:v:pref,nolink}
This is one possible verb to use with {watrIn:n}.[2]

definition: travel or move a specified or measurable distance or trajectory
definition_fr: voyager ou se déplacer une distance ou une trajectoire spécifiée ou mesurable
notes: The object of this verb is the distance or range of motion. It is used with movement verbs such as {ron:v:1}.
This is used for passengers only, and would not be used for "riding" a bicycle, for example.[3]
This is also called {lIghonya':n:nolink}, typically by older speakers.[1, p.141-142]
This is often pronounced as if it were {lIghongan:n:nolink}[1, p.141]
This means to begin to sing a song (the singer is the subject and the song is the object).[1]

definition_fr: simuler, imiter, se faire passer pour
notes: The idea is that the subject of the verb looks or behaves like something (or someone) else or represents something (or someone) else. Like {ghet:v}, it has no connotation of fraud or anything underhanded. The object is the thing being simulated or the person being impersonated.

This is something (or someone) which looks or behaves like something (or someone) else. A {lIlwI':n:nolink} is different from a {lIw:n} since {lIw:n:nolink} implies replacement, whereas a {lIlwI':n:nolink} doesn't replace anyone or anything.

When {A:sen:nolink} and {B:sen:nolink} share {C:sen:nolink} with each other, the construction is {C lulIn A B je:sen:nolink} (or {C lIn A B je:sen:nolink} if {C:sen:nolink} is plural). In this case, the speaker is non-committal about whether {A:sen:nolink} or {B:sen:nolink} is the one who decided to do the sharing with the other.[1] When a computer (or computer system) is online, it's said to be "sharing". See {lIn:v:2}.

definition_fr: aller en ligne (se connecter au réseau informatique)
notes: This is just the application of {lIn:v:1} to a computer networking context. Klingons think of a computer (or computer system) which is online as "sharing".
This idiomatic expression is not a euphemism, but is a little risque. It means that the subjects have a physical relationship of some sort.
While this can apply to fires, it is more common to use {chenmoH:v} or {vemmoH:v:2} in that case.[2]
Large game animal indigenous to {Qo'noS:n}.

definition: be creative, be inventive, be resourceful
definition_fr: être créatif, être inventif, être ingénieux
notes: To be imaginative, innovative, original, or inspired; to generate novel ideas, recognize patterns that are not obvious to others, or use existing things in non-traditional ways.[1]

definition_fr: sécher, être bloqué (mentalement, sur un problème)
notes: This means being stuck like when you can't solve an algebra problem or a crossword puzzle.
She is a follower of {tIquvma:n:name}.
source: [1] {DSC - Battle at the Binary Stars:src}, [2] {Saarbrücken qepHom'a' 2019:src}

notes: This refers to research methods/techniques for doing studies.[1]
This animal is more rat-sized than mouse-sized, but a {vIghro':n} might well chase it. Its face kind of resembles that of a bat (though a bat is not a rodent).[1]
This is something constructed to hold a door or gate, whether a door or gate is there or not.
This refers to a group of igneous rocks composed primarily of feldspar and quartz.

This refers to a temporary substitute or stand-in. To denote a permanent replacement, use {qa'meH:n}.[2] To refer to something or someone which simulates or impersonates something or someone else, without replacement, see {lIlwI':n}.[4]

notes: This applies to full words only, not prefixes (which are {moHaq:n}).

The cultural connotations are a bit different than the English word "concubine". In Klingon culture, everything associated with a {lIwnal:n:nolink} lacks honor, which is not necessarily the case for a (Terran) king's concubines or courtesans. Only married people could have a partner who could be considered a {lIwnal:n:nolink}. A {lIwnal:n:nolink} could be male or female, so if it's necessary to distinguish, use {loD lIwnal:n@@loD:n, lIwnal:n} or {be' lIwnal:n@@be':n, lIwnal:n}.
This could mean "download" or "upload", depending on the context.
This refers to a state of matter.
This refers to hair on the upper lip.[2] For "growing" a mustache, the verb {nargh:v:2} is used.[3]

definition: be a fraction of, make up a portion of, constitute part of
definition_fr: être une fraction de, constituer une partie de, former une portion de
notes: This is used to express fractions in math. If appropriate in a mathematical discussion, no prefix is used even if the denominator is one, even though this is a bit grammatically aberrant. (One would not say {wa' luloch wej:sen@@wa':n:num, lu-:v, loch:v, wej:n:num}.)[1]
The suffix for the plural of this word depends on whether it is used to refer to beings capable of language (see {-pu':n:suff}) or not (see {-mey:n:suff}).

definition: I am not a merry man.
definition_fr: Je ne suis pas un homme joyeux.

notes: A "brother-in-law" is {loDnI' loDnal:n@@loDnI':n, loDnal:n} or {be'nI' loDnal:n@@be'nI':n, loDnal:n}.
In Klingon, "deep space" is called {logh Hop:n}, literally, "far space".[3]

definition_fr: fois, nombre de fois (suffixe de répétition)
notes: This is appended to a number to form an adverbial meaning that many times. For example, {wa'logh:adv} "once, one time" from {wa':n:num} "one", {cha'logh:adv} "twice, two times" from {cha':n:num} "two", and so on.

notes: This is the name of a Federation space station.
This refers to the upper front of the torso.[1]

This is an extension of {logh'ob:n:1} to the front of other things, in which case the back would be {Sa'Hut:n:2} and the sides would be {reD:n:3}.[1] In this usage, the plural is formed with {-mey:n:suff}.[2] This can apply to cars, motorcycles, space ships and the like, but not to the front of a computer screen (too flat) or a bottle (because it's round). There's an overlap with {'et:n:2h}, but whereas {'et:n:2h,nolink} refers to a 3-dimensional space, {logh'ob:n:2,nolink} refers to the surface at the front.[3]
This refers to the central processing unit of a computer.

This word is used for something that incrementally or gradually (not necessarily slowly) goes away, such as food on one's plate or dirt that one washes off of something.[2] If a room is filled with boxes that are to be taken somewhere, and then over a short or long time, the boxes are removed, then {loj:v:nolink} could be used once there are no more boxes. If a room was full of furniture, and a person left the room and came back to find the room empty (and there was no reason to expect this to happen), then {ngab:v} might be used.[2] This word would be appropriate to describe what happens to someone who beams away, if one is focusing on the incremental disappearance of the person. Once the person is gone, {ngab:v:nolink} might be used. People who are watching someone beam away might use {DemchoH:v@@Dem:v, -choH:v} to describe what they are seeing.[2]

definition: No one eavesdrops at an open door.

notes: {lojmItjaj:n:nolink} tends to be used on formal occasions, while both it and {ghInjaj:n:nolink} are used, seemingly indiscriminately, otherwise.

definition: be in a stance, be in a pose (people, animals, or martial arts)
definition_fr: être dans une position, être dans une pose (personnes, animaux ou arts martiaux)
notes: The verb to use for striking a pose or stance is {much:v:3}.

Note that there is a homophonous verb {lol:v:1} which can be applied to people or animals. Some of the verb suffixes have a precise meaning when used with this verb, when it is applied to aircraft or spacecraft: ▶ {lolchu':v} "be in a correct attitude" ▶ {lolchu'taH:v} "maintain a correct attitude" ▶ {lolmoH:v} "maneuver (an aircraft) to be in an attitude" ▶ {loltaH:v} "maintain an attitude"

definition: a specific position in the martial arts form Mok'bara
definition_fr: une position spécifique dans la forme d'arts martiaux Mok'bara
notes: This refers to a specific martial arts stance, and is not a general term for "stance", for which see {tonSaw':n}.[2]

definition_fr: manœuvrer (un avion) ​​pour être dans une attitude

notes: This word is plural. Its singular form is unknown. It appears to consist of the elements {lol:v:2}, {SeH:v}, and {cha:n}, or homophones thereof.

notes: This term is used even if no celebration ({lop:n}) is involved.[1]

definition: party, celebration (a specific type of Klingon party or celebration)
definition_fr: fête, célébration (un type spécifique de fête ou de célébration Klingon)
notes: This is an event to which the spirits of ancestors are invited.[2]

definition: A warrior does not complain about physical discomfort.
definition_fr: Un guerrier ne se plaint pas d'inconfort physique.

notes: Consider using the suffix {-qu':v:suff}.
This refers to formerly living things, and not, for example, to volcanoes.[1]
This word refers to one's mother's brother's child or one's father's sister's child (i.e., "cross-cousin").
For a man, this word refers to a child of his sister. For a woman, this word refers to a child of her brother.

A female {lor:n:0}, that is, a cousin who is one's mother's brother's daughter or one's father's sister's daughter, or a niece in the sense of a man's sister's daughter or a woman's brother's daughter.
A male {lor:n:0}, that is, a cousin who is one's mother's brother's son or one's father's sister's son, or a nephew in the sense of a man's sister's son or a woman's brother's son.

definition: fourth tone of nonatonic musical scale
definition_fr: quatrième note de la gamme musicale nonatonique
notes: The tones of the Klingon musical scale (see {yutlhegh:n}) are: {yu:n}, {bIm:n}, {'egh:n}, {loS:n:2,nolink}, {vagh:n:2}, {jav:n:2}, {Soch:n:2}, {chorgh:n:2}, {yu:n:nolink}.
The verb usually associated with this is {qaS:v}.[1]
Quadrotriticale is a four-lobed hybridization of wheat (genus Triticum) and rye (genus Secale).
This word and {Qugh:n:1h,nolink} are mostly interchangeable. To refer to something that in all likelihood one can't recover from (like the loss of {pIraqSIS:n}), {lot:n:nolink} is better.[2]
Informally, some people say {'Iw Doy':n}.[1]

definition: a bird that swoops into the water in order to catch food, but cannot swim
definition_fr: un oiseau qui plonge dans l'eau pour attraper de la nourriture, mais ne sait pas nager

notes: A planet in the Cardassian Union.

definition: have personality, be charismatic, be charming
definition_fr: avoir de la personnalité, être charismatique, être charmant

notes: This can be used for "mode" in the sense of a mode of usage. For example, "night mode" (a mode in software to turn its user interface dark, for use at night) would be {ram lo':n@@ram:n, lo':n}.[2]
This preceeds the noun it modifies.
This is a simple verb in its own right, and not the verb {lo':v} with the suffix {-laH:v}. It's likely that there is a historical connection to the verb plus suffix form.[2]
See {chetvI':n:1} for an idiom related to worthlessness.

definition_fr: tomber (en disgrâce, subir une perte de statut)
notes: See {pum:v:2} for a literal fall. {lu qeng:n:name,nolink} "The Fall of Kang" is a famous poem by G'trok.[1, p.107]

{chaH:n}/{bIH:n}:{ghaH:n}/{'oH:n} = {lu-:v:pref,nolink} When used with {-lu':v}, this prefix means "Someone (indefinite subject) does something to them". This prefix is sometimes dropped for unknown reasons. While an error, this is often overlooked when clarity is not an issue, except in formal situations.[2]
This refers to a geometric figure that is self-similar at all scales, or to any object, system, or idea that exhibits this property.[1]

There is an idiom, {lugh; Sor rur}.[2] This is used for someone who makes a correct statement, or does something which is proper, appropriate, justified, or acceptable. That is, it means "factually correct" or "morally correct". It isn't used, for example, for a switch which is doing what it's supposed to do, for which see {mIt:v}. It also isn't used for a truthful fact or statement itself, for which see {teH:v} and {qar:v}.[3]

This is used for pulling when the pulling is sudden or done with a jerk. This verb can generally be used where either {Hur:v} or {Hoq:v} might otherwise be used, but not in the case of pulling back a bowstring.[2]

definition: cause (someone) to confess or reveal a secret
definition_fr: faire (quelqu'un) avouer ou révéler un secret

notes: In ascending order of ferocity, the verbs used to describe military confrontations are: {Qor:v}, {tlhaS:v}, {vay:v}, {lul:v:nolink}, {Hargh:v}.

definition_fr: reporter, remettre à plus tard, procrastiner

notes: A plant whose seeds are rendered into a powder or paste to produce a condiment or spice.[1]
While this is an anatomy term, it can be used for other things, such as wood which has gotten wet.

definition_fr: type d'animal, loung (ressemblant à un lézard)

This is the most technical term, but there are also the slang expressions {ghew Duj:n} and {jIrwI' Duj:n}.[1]

In some contexts, it's more common to express the location (stated in units of {lawrI'(mey):n@@lawrI':n, -mey:n}, though the word itself is optional) followed by {ngotrI':n} and/or {lungrI':n:nolink} without a verb. This is a form of clipped Klingon.[1]
This refers to the imaginary lines used in determining coordinates (or the actual lines drawn on a map or similar image).[1]

definition_fr: ligne de coordonnées (système de coordonnées traditionnel)

The Klingon compass has three points, rather than four: {chan:n} (east), {'ev:n} (northwest), and {tIng:n} (southwest). The areas around an object are its {Dung:n} (area above), {bIng:n} (area below), {retlh:n} (area beside), {tlhop:n:1} (front), and {'em:n} (behind). Something in an object's {retlh:n:nolink} can be on its {poS:n} (left) or its {nIH:n} (right). The area between two objects are their {joj:n} (area between). The area beyond an object is its {Hay:n:2h}. In standard Klingon, locative nouns follow pronouns, e.g., {jIH tlhop:n:nolink} "in front of me". But in the dialect of the Sakrej region ({Sa'Qej Sep:n}), locative nouns take pronominal possessive suffixes, e.g., {tlhopwIj:n:nolink} "my area in front".[2] However, the directional nouns are an exception to this rule, and take possessive suffixes in every known dialect, e.g., {chanwIj:n:nolink} "east of me, to my east". If the full pronoun is used with a directional noun, the pronoun is emphasized, e.g., {jIH chan:n:nolink} "east of ME, to MY east".[4] When referring to one's left and right sides, possessive suffixes are used. For example, one might say {nIHwIj ghop:n@@nIH:n, -wIj:n, ghop:n} to refer to their right hand.[5] The points in between the three cardinal directions are {tIng chan:n:nolink}, {'ev chan:n:nolink}, and either {tIng 'ev:n:nolink} or {'ev tIng:n:nolink}. {chan:n:nolink} always comes second in such a compound.[3]

This noun indicates that a single thing is being considered apart from others, or that a sequence of identical things is considered one after another. In contexts where it refers to multiple things, it can be translated as "each X". When {Hoch:n:nolink} precedes a noun which isn't explicitly plural, it also means "each X". The difference is that {Hoch:n:nolink} focuses on things as members of a group, whereas {ngIq:n:nolink} focuses on the individual things. It's a subtle difference, but a difference nonetheless. In such contexts, {ngIq:n:nolink} has a sequential meaning (whereas {Hoch:n:nolink} does not).[4] In some contexts, {ngIq:n:nolink} can be translated as "single" or "individual", but it always implies that there are (or could be) other similar things. This word literally means "fiery lava" on Krios. It implies courage of a surprising or unexpected kind, perhaps even recklessness (unlike {toDuj:n} which is more neutral).[1, p.10]
This can be used to describe corrupt people.[2]

Klingon has no word for "color" in the sense of "what color is that?" or "red is a nice color". This word is used to distinguish between, for example, a color photograph and a black-and-white photograph.[2]
For an anatomical skeleton, see {nobmeD:n}, although {Hom qal'aq:n@@Hom:n:1, qal'aq:n} and {porgh qal'aq:n@@porgh:n, qal'aq:n} are also fine.
The parts of a foot include its {bem:n} "sole", {va'nuch:n} "heel", {mov:n} "top (of foot)", and {yaD:n:1} "toe(s)". The foot is attached to the {'uS:n} "leg" through the {ngIb:n:1} "ankle".
This is what Klingons would call a Terran bicycle.

According to legend, this is the name of an ancient village on {Qo'noS:n} where {qeylIS'e' lIjlaHbe'bogh vay':n:name} and {luqara':n:name} fought a great battle against hundreds of enemies, a major component of their courtship.

Note that in Klingon, there is a different word for "be old (not new)" ({ngo':v}) than for "be old (not young)" ({qan:v:1,nolink}). Also, "old" in the sense of "former" is {Deq:v}. This word is applied to people and animals.[2]

definition_fr: utilise le petit doigt, le petit doigt
notes: An idiomatic gesture (due to homophony with {qan:v:1}): to point your pinkie at someone is to comment that you believe they are old.
Note that {qanwI':n:nolink} can also mean "old person". An idiomatic gesture: to point your pinkie at someone is to comment that you believe they are old.
He is the father of {qeylIS'e' lIjlaHbe'bogh vay':n:name} and {moratlh:n:name}.
This is the name of a sentient species native to {qanQIy loS:n}.

definition: a bird known for its song
definition_fr: un oiseau connu pour son chant

notes: According to the {paq'batlh:src}, he was the Patriarch ({qup'a':n}) of {qamchIy:n:place} at the time of {qeylIS'e' lIjlaHbe'bogh vay':n:name}.

definition: always agree with, always cooperate with
definition_fr: toujours d'accord avec, toujours coopérer avec

This is the closest Klingon equivalent.
This verb is used in forming tag questions with the suffix {-'a':v:suff}. In such a question, {qar'a':sen:nolink} either follows the verb, or comes at the end of the sentence. ({TKDA 6.4:src})

This means "Oh, yeah?" in the sense of "Is that so?" (For example, in response to "I just heard some interesting news", one might respond "Oh, yeah? What is it?")[1] For "oh, yeah?" as an expression of disbelief or defiance, see {bItaHrup'a'?:sen}

definition: Fire the torpedoes at my command!
definition_fr: Tirez les torpilles à mon commandement !

notes: The Cardassian Homeworld, the main planet of the Cardassian Union. Also called {qarDaSya':n:nolink}[1, p.141-142] and {qarDaS wa':n:nolink} (Cardassia Prime)[2].
This refers to a convex quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel sides. A quadrilateral with no parallel sides is a {moHbey:n}.
Some people pluralize this word with {-pu':n:suff}, but most use {-mey:n:suff}.

definition: bird capable of mimicking speech, larger than {qaryoq:n}
definition_fr: oiseau capable d'imiter la parole, plus grand que {qaryoq:n}
notes: Some people pluralize this word with {-pu':n:suff}, but most use {-mey:n:suff}.

definition: Four thousand throats may be cut in one night by a running man.
definition_fr: Quatre mille gorges peuvent être tranchées en une nuit par un homme qui court.
par heure (par exemple, distance par heure)
