definition: The dishonor of the father dishonors his sons and their sons for three generations.
definition_fr: Le déshonneur du père déshonore ses fils et leurs fils pendant trois générations.
search_tags: The dishonour of the father dishonours his sons and their sons for three generations.

notes: {qaSuj'a'?:sen:nolink} is how you would ask the question if you're speaking to only one person. To ask a group of people if you're disturbing them, say {SaSuj'a'?:sen:nolink} "Am I disturbing you (plural)?"
The subject wraps or encases the object.[2, p.76]

definition_fr: accompagner (chanter) avec de la musique instrumentale
notes: Most Klingon music is vocal. When there is an instrumental component to a song, the players are said to {qat:v:2,nolink} the song.[2, p.76]
This is just the Klingon pronunciation of a Vulcan word.
This is a more common (and nerdier) term for {venwI':n:nolink}.

definition: shellfish (clam, oyster, mussel, scallop, brachiopod, etc.)
definition_fr: crustacés (palourde, huître, moule, pétoncle, brachiopode, etc.)
notes: There are a number of these sorts of creatures. This word applies to various bivalves. Large {qatvoHmey:n@@qatvoH:n, -mey:n} are served in non-Klingon restaurants that feature Klingon food, but they usually just call this dish "Jumbo Klingon Mollusks".[1]
Though commonly used for a water pipe, a {qatlhDa':n} need not be restricted to water, nor even to liquids.[1]

This word is used in {Klingon Monopoly:src} to denote how many {QaS:n:1h} a player has to pay when landing on a planet owned by another player.[1] It's not clear what {qav:v:hyp,nolink} means by itself, but it's possible that this was shortened from {qavmeH 'ap:n:nolink} or something like that at some point in the past.[2]

This refers to "memory" in the sense of the ability to remember or the power of recall. It does not refer to specific memories or recollections, for which see {wov'on:n}. Someone who has an excellent memory may be said to have a {qaw pov:n@@qaw:n, pov:v}.

definition_fr: banques de mémoire, banques de données
notes: This word is singular.[2] The first part of this word is {qaw:n}, but the second part has nothing to do with surgery (see {Haq:v:1}). The resemblance is just a coincidence.[3]

definition_fr: mal se souvenir, se souvenir incorrectement

notes: The subject does the reminding, the object is the thing remembered, and the person who is reminded is marked with {-vaD:n}. It seems that for some verbs {X:sen:nolink} which take an object, when {-moH:v} is added to such a verb, the resulting bivalent verb {XmoH:sen:nolink} takes the same object, while the original subject of {X:sen:nolink} becomes the beneficiary of {XmoH:sen:nolink} and is marked with {-vaD:n}. However, this pattern does not hold for all such verbs, and in particular does not hold for {tuQmoH:v}.[3]
source: [1] {TKD:src}, [2] {SkyBox S20:src} (reprinted in {HQ 5.2, p.14, Jun. 1996:src}), [3] {KLI mailing list 2022.05.20:src}

notes: This is a gathering or ceremony to remember and honor someone who has died.[1]

This would be used if something tipped over on its own accord or seemingly on its own accord (even if there is a known cause). For example, this would be used if one lost one's balance. For "flip (all the way) over", see {yoymoH:v} and {tach:v}.[2]

definition: tip over, knock over, knock down
notes: If something is made to fall rather than simply tip over, {pummoH:v@@pum:v:2, -moH:v} may be more appropriate.[1] {qaw'moH:v:nolink} is also used for turning the pages of a book.[2]
This is a proposed regulation or rule or law, not one enacted or implemented or enforceable yet.[1]

definition: be a problem, be a hassle
definition_fr: être un problème, être un tracas

notes: The subject does the replacing, and the object is replaced. This verb seems to have been derived from {qa'meH:n}, possibly through misinterpretation of what was originally the suffix {-qa':v}. This verb is used with {ngutlh:n:nolink} (see {ngutlhmey qa':sen}) to express the concept of transliteration.[2]
This refers to a sort of life force within a person which escapes when that person dies.[2] It takes the plural suffix {-pu':n:suff}.[1, p.117]

definition: We fight to enrich the spirit.
definition_fr: Nous nous battons pour enrichir l'esprit.

notes: This word was originally a shortened form of {quvqa'meH:sen:nolink} (see {qa'meH vIttlhegh:n}), but has since become accepted as a noun in its own right. It refers to something that takes over for or is used instead of something that is gone or which has been lost. To denote a temporary substitute or stand-in, use {lIw:n}.[2]
These are a set of proverbs used to restore respect or credibility after one has been embarrassed in a public setting.[2] In the past, this used to be {quvqa'meH vIttlhegh:n:nolink}.[1]
This is used for a minor software update (e.g., 2.0 to 2.1).
Its claw is eaten. This word may also be spelled {Qa'raj:n:nolink}. Do not confuse this with the similarly named {Qaj:n}.

definition: end (of corridor, tunnel, conduit, Jeffries tube, sewer, road, bridge, long field, etc.)
definition_fr: extrémité (de couloir, tunnel, conduit, tube Jeffries, égout, route, pont, champ long, etc.)
notes: This refers to both (or all) ends of any longish enclosed space that one is typically inside of or experiences from the inside, or a bounded space which is seen as having length even if not enclosed. A {qa'rI':n:nolink} at or from which one can enter or exit (into an enclosed space) is a {DIn:n}.[2]
This is a person able to make contact with the world of spirits.[1]
It is much larger than a {notqa':n}.

This is the Klingon code name for the Federation's Genesis weapons research project.[2] The word itself means "origin of everything" or "start of it all" or the like, and refers to the beginning of the universe. Unlike its English translation, the Klingon term doesn't contain the notion of an explosion.[3]

definition: qa'vak (traditional game), game played with hoop and stick
definition_fr: qa'vak (jeu traditionnel), jeu joué avec un cerceau et un bâton
notes: The idiom {vIHtaH gho:sen} comes from this activity.
This seems to have been taken from the Federation Standard word "caffeine".[1]
This refers to the action of squeezing the bag part of the {DIron:n}, usually with the elbow.[1, p.76]
This is the 3rd element of the periodic table.

definition_fr: cuve, tonneau (pour le stockage de l'alcool)
pardonner, ne pas ressentir de ressentiment
notes: In the {paq'raD:n:nolink} "Force Book" of the {paq'batlh:n}, the second section is titled {qeHHa' loDnI':sen:nolink}, which is given the somewhat loose English translation "A Brother's Forgiveness". A footnote explains that the concept of forgiveness does not map exactly to Klingon culture, and that the literal meaning of the title is "A Brother Unresents". The title of the corresponding canto in the opera {'u':src} is {loDnI'Daj quvqa'moH:sen:nolink}, literally, "he causes the brother to have honor again".

This means lower the head slightly whether or not the head is again raised. So, among other things, it can refer to nodding to the beat of music or nodding off (falling asleep). The subject might be, for example, {nach:n} "head" (even though this might be considered redundant) or the nodder. It does not take an object.[1] This verb refers only to the motion, not what such a motion may or may not indicate. To express that the nodding means something, such as agreement, use {Qochbe':v} with this verb. In some cultures, nodding may indicate something other than agreement, so one might use {yaj:v} with this verb. See the examples.[2]

definition: Kal'Hyah (ritual undertaken by groom before marriage)
definition_fr: Kal'Hyah (rituel entrepris par le marié avant le mariage)
notes: This is a "mental and spiritual journey" that a Klingon groom undertakes with his closest male friends. It lasts four days and the fasting participants are required to endure six trials: deprivation, blood, pain, sacrifice, anguish, and death. It has been inaccurately referred to as a "Klingon bachelor party".
This is a unit of measurement roughly akin to two kilometers.
This is a humanoid species from {qa'mInar:n}. They share the planet with another sentient species, the Ba'ul.
source: [1] {DSC - Si Vis Pacem, Para Bellum:src}, [2] {Saarbrücken qepHom'a' 2019:src}
[1] {DSC - Si Vis Pacem, Para Bellum:src}, [2] {Saarbrücken qepHom'a' 2019:src}

notes: This refers to a cultural or societal ancestor or forebearer (who is not necessarily related by blood). For a direct ancestor, see {'emrIgh:n}.[2]

definition: Qempa'keh, the Warriors of the Dead
notes: These are the enraged ({QeH:v}) ancestral spirits ({qempa':n}) populating {ghe'tor:n}.[1] This word is a fossilized form. It refers to a unique group, the "proudest spirits of Gre'thor". Generally speaking, this word wouldn't be pluralized (but behaves grammatically like a plural).[2]

definition_fr: récemment, il y a peu de temps

notes: This means to move an object over something while maintaining contact, with the intention of removing some substance from the surface. The object is the surface being wiped. If something is used to do the wiping, the verb {lo':v} is used with it as the object. If something is wiped away, the verb {bI':v} is used with that as the object.[1]
A pregnant woman is said to {qeng:v:nolink} a {puq:n}.[2] See {yatlh:v}.
Played by {mayqel 'anSara':n:name}.

The best translation is determined by context. If there's a lot of stuff, the plural form {qengHoDmey:n@@qengHoD:n, -mey:n} is often (but not necessarily) used. The resemblance to "Captain Kang" ({qeng HoD:n@@qeng:n, HoD:n}) is coincidental, but even so, Kang's crew was careful to never say {qengHoDmey:n:nolink} when he was around.

definition: annual meeting of Klingon speakers in Germany
definition_fr: réunion annuelle des locuteurs klingons en Allemagne
notes: The {qepHom'a':n:nolink} is the annual Klingon Language meeting in Saarbrücken ({Sarbruqen:n}), Germany. Please visit their website at {www.qepHom.de:url:http://www.qepHom.de/} for more information. The official annual conference of the Klingon Language Institute is known as the {qep'a':n}, while other gatherings of Klingonists are known as {qepHommey:n:nolink}. The meeting in Saarbrücken, Germany, is the largest {qepHom:n:nolink} (and it sometimes even has more participants than the {qep'a':n:nolink}). For this reason, it is called {qepHom'a':n:nolink}. Its name contains an intentional ungrammaticality: two type 1 noun suffixes.
The {qep'a':n:nolink} is the official annual conference of the Klingon Language Institute ({tlhIngan Hol yejHaD:n}).
Also related are the suffixes {-rup:v} and {-beH:v}. To train really well, to work really hard at it and achieve intended goals, would be {qeqchu':v@@qeq:v, -chu':v}.[2]

definition_fr: annuler la réduction (revenir à la taille d'origine)

notes: This refers to a specific place in the house for heating or food preparation.
This is the name of a book. The famous author {Qa'taq:n:name} wrote a commentary on this work.
This is a Klingon animal which eats vegetation, and also small animals and birds. Klingons might eat them, but mostly consider them pests.
This is the closest Klingon equivalent.
This is sauce prepared by thickening {chanDoq:n}.

This grows on certain kinds of trees and looks much like a pine cone as seen on Earth. It contains genetic material, so it's similar in function to a pine cone as well. This is the proper term, but the term {Sor 'IventoH:n@@Sor:n, 'IventoH:n} "tree pineapple" is also heard. The Terran pine cone (or, more generally, conifer cone) should be called {tera' qet'uy:n@@tera':n, qet'uy:n}[1] or {tera' qIrqoD qet'uy:n@@tera':n, qIrqoD:n, qet'uy:n}.[2]
This is a traded commodity, like {DIlyum:n}.
This refers to the entire system including the vulva.

Kahless is the legendary first Klingon Emperor, who united the Klingon people. There are two versions of his title. The older version, {qeylIS lIjlaHbogh pagh:n:name@@qeylIS:n, lIj:v, -laH:v, -bogh:v, pagh:n:1}, is applied to Kahless only, while the newer version {qeylIS'e' lIjlaHbe'bogh vay':n:name,nolink} may be applied to Kahless and other leaders/heroes as well. It would be a sign of extreme arrogance or disrespect to use the older version for anyone other than Kahless.[2] His return is prophesied in the Story of the Promise, which states that: ▶ {ghIq chalDaq HovDaq SIq qeylIS 'ej jatlh pa' DaqHomvetlh wovDaq HInej.:sen}
source: [1] {SkyBox S8:src} (reprinted in {HQ 4.3, p.4-5, Sep. 1995:src}), [2] {paq'batlh 2ed:src} ({KLI mailing list 2021.10.10:src})

notes: This is abbreviated QB in the {paq'batlh:src}.
This is abbreviated QBV in the {paq'batlh:src}.

definition: Eyes of Kahless, a game played with dice
definition_fr: Eyes of Kahless, un jeu qui se joue avec des dés
notes: This is a guessing game with dice in which the winner receives a punch.
All fermented meat is known as {qeyvaq Ha'DIbaH:n:nolink}, with the word for the specific meat replacing the word {Ha'DIbaH:n:1}.
The Intracluster Medium is the very hot, low-density, diffuse plasma in between galaxies inside a galaxy cluster.[1]

definition: joke, make a joke, tell a joke
notes: This verb normally doesn't take an object (unless one is playing word games or something). To state the joke, {jatlh:v} would normally be used.[2] To play a practical joke on someone isn't {qID:v:nolink}, but {chem:v}.[3]
This verb always takes an object or {-chuq:v} in normal usage.[2]

definition_fr: ignorer, ne pas prendre en compte

notes: This is the general word for a season. For example, {qImroq tuj:n@@qImroq:n, tuj:v} would be something like "summer" on Earth.[1]
This is the name of a city, where {qeylIS'e' lIjlaHbe'bogh vay':n:name} once witnessed a foolish man stand outside the walls during a fierce storm in an attempt to make the wind respect him.

This is a tool resembling a sickle. It's for agriculture, but, of course, it could be used as a weapon. If it has a long handle, "scythe" may be a better translation, though it's not quite either of them.

definition_fr: frapper (avec la main, le poing, un outil)
notes: This can be used for knocking (on a door, etc.).[2]
Klingon hygienic practices do not focus on cleanliness, though this is not ruled out, either.[1]

definition_fr: un arbre aux feuilles en forme d'aiguilles
notes: It is reasonable to use {tera' qIrqoD:n:nolink} for the "pine" tree.
There are also various slang terms: {Huy:v:3}, {roSbe':v}, {jIr qIvon:sen}, {wamtaH:sen}.[1]
While this word is known only as the name of a ship class, it seems likely that it also refers to a bird or to a class of predatory birds (cf. {toQ:n}).

This is a big, fat bird native to Kronos, which is able to fly, but not for a long time. A female one of these is a {qItbe':n:nolink}, while a male is a {qItloD:n:nolink}.[2] It resembles a Terran guineafowl.[1]
{qor:n:name}'s left {qIvon:n:nolink} would ache whenever his ship hit warp eight.[3] Maltz seemed reluctant to talk about what exactly this is.[2]

Klingons don't have euphemisms for going to the bathroom, and would just use {ghIm:v} with {turmIq:n}, {qeQ:n}, or {taQbang:n:2}. However, this slang expression or idiom is used from time to time, though mostly (but hardly always) by or to children. One might ask a jittery child, {belHa''a' qIvonlIj?:sen@@belHa':v, -'a':v, qIvon:n, -lIj:n} Most people say {qIvon:n} but some say {qIvonDu':n@@qIvon:n, -Du':n}.[2]
This is used for praying to a religious or similar figure.[1]

This verb is used for signing a treaty, contract, loan agreement, etc. It can also be used for signing up for an account to use a service (see {qI':v:2}), registering for a conference or class or even auditions for a team or a show. It can also be used for signing a petition. The underlying meaning is that something (an obligation, commitment, pact, response, or arrangement of some sort) comes about as a result of the signing. The object of this verb is the document which is signed.[2] In contrast, when one signs an autograph, there is no commitment or response involved. The verb to use in that situation is {tlhI':v:nolink}.[2]

definition: register for, sign up for (an account)
notes: This is an extension of {qI':v:1} to mean signing up for an account to use a service. The typical object of this verb is {mab:n:2}.
This refers to a person, and isn't the word to use when referring to the other half of a pair of socks or gloves or the like, for which see {nelwI':n}.[2]
The object of this verb is the space being squeezed into, such as a small car or crowded elevator, or clothes or shoes that are too small.
This refers to the gummy material.

This both holds up one's {yopwaH:n} and is used for hanging weapons.[2] {qoghmey:n:nolink} generally means "belts", but could also mean "ears scattered all about", due to the homophony with {qogh:n:2}. This homophony is also the basis of a slang expression, {qogh tuQmoHHa':sen}.[3]

This refers to the external flap of skin, cartilage, or whatever. The internal organ of hearing is called {teS:n}. {qoghDu':n:nolink} can only mean "ears", while {qoghmey:n:nolink} is usually the plural of {qogh:n:1} and means "belts". The homophony between these two words is the basis of a slang expression, {qogh tuQmoHHa':sen}.[2]

This expression literally means "take off one's belt". It derives its slang meaning from the homophony between {qogh:n:1} and {qogh:n:2}.[1] The unusual suffix placement ({tuQmoHHa':v:nolink} rather than {tuQHa'moH:v}) occurs in this idiom only.[2]
Watch Gowron say this: {YouTube video:url:http://youtu.be/FJ7HlgaTt44}

definition: The wind does not respect a fool.
definition_fr: Le vent ne respecte pas un imbécile.

notes: When connecting multiple sentences, only the final conjunction is needed. See the example.
This is used to refer to articulation, and does not have the sense of "proclaim, declare, decree".

definition: collection of segments that are joined together, collocation
notes: This word refers to the entire collection of joined things, not to an individual component. Its components don't have to be physically joined, but they have to have a connection or be arranged as if they were or could be joined. The difference between this word and {vey:n} is that a deck of playing cards (in any order) would be an {'echletHom vey:n}, whereas if the cards were organized by suit, and within each suit the cards were in numerical order, then not only would there be an {'echletHom vey:n:nolink}, but there would be four {'echletHom qolmey:n@@'echletHom:n, qol:n:1h, -mey:n}.[1]
He is a member of the House of Kor ({qor tuq:n:name}).
source: [1] {DSC - Battle at the Binary Stars:src}, [2] {Saarbrücken qepHom'a' 2019:src}

definition: core, essence (e.g., main members of a group of people)
definition_fr: noyau, essence (par exemple, les principaux membres d'un groupe de personnes)
notes: This can refer to the core of a group of people.
To prepare this, {tap:v} a mixture of {naH:n} and animal matter, and let {rogh:v}.

This word is used for the act of composing songs, stories, etc.[2, p.71] Klingons consider songs as things which just exist, and the act of composition is viewed as hunting down, trapping, and logging them.[3] There is another verb, {gher:v}, which is used for compiling lists and the like, and which, in contrast to {qon:v:nolink}, suggests that information is merely passed along.[4]
Note that {qonwI':n:nolink} can also mean a recording device, as in {mIllogh qonwI':n}.
This is a Klingon legume whose seeds grow underground. For the Terran peanut, precede with {tera':n}.[1]
This is a type of intrusive igneous rock formed by slow cooling of magma.[1]
Played by {jan qalI'qoS:n:name}.
This is the House of {qol:n:2,name} and, of course, {qor:n:name}.
source: [1] {DSC - The Butcher's Knife Cares Not for the Lamb's Cry:src}
[1] {TKD:src}, [2] {SkyBox S13:src} (reprinted in {HQ 4.3, p.4-5, Sep. 1995:src}), [3] {SkyBox S20:src} (reprinted in {HQ 5.2, p.14, Jun. 1996:src}), [4] {KLI mailing list 2020.08.17:src}

notes: Unlike {teb:v:1}, this indicates stopping up an opening, but not filling up the inside.
This word refers to the cork or stopper of a bottle, such as a wine bottle.[1] It can also be used for the device some Humans use to keep their babies quiet (which is not a Klingon custom).[2]

According to Klingon legend, Kortar was the first Klingon. He and his mate slew the gods, and he now ferries the souls of the dishonored to Gre'thor ({ghe'tor:n}) on the Barge of the Dead ({Hegh Duj:n}).
According to legend, this is the name of a Klingon who committed murder while his victim was sleeping. His name is synonymous with cowardice.[1]
According to the glossary to {A Burning House:src}, this is a rodent that is considered a destructive pest on Klingon farms, where farmers have to set traps for them.
This is an Earth plant. There is, however, a parsley-like plant that grows on {Qo'noS:n} called {rebmub:n}.[1]
These are pale, serpent-like creatures which inhabit the waters crossed by the Barge of the Dead ({Hegh Duj:n}) on its way to Gre'thor ({ghe'tor:n}).
This word refers to form rather than function.[2] It may be thought of as a flat version of {SIrgh:n}.[3]

definition: back, sponsor, support, capitalize, invest in
definition_fr: soutenir, parrainer, appuyer, capitaliser, investir dans
notes: To specify what or how much is invested, make use of {peS:v}, as in {X qotmeH Y peS:sen:nolink} "invest Y in X".[1]
Though there is a noun, the idea of raising a number to the power of something is generally expressed by using the verb {Sep:v:2}.[1]

definition_fr: petite créature ressemblant à un chien
notes: This is a creature like Kruge's pet (see {Qugh:n:2,name}).
This is a group of three, something with three members or three parts.[1]
The first part is just the transliteration of the English word "cola".
A planet in the Federation.

'aqroS ...:sen}.[1] This word is also used in mathematics as a short form of {ra'Duch leD qubbID:n} (see {qubbID:n:2}).[2]

A common way to express lighting or starting a fire is with {chenmoH:v}. Another way to express igniting and extinguishing a fire is with {vemmoH:v:0} "wake up, cause to wake up" and {QongmoH:v:0} "put to sleep, cause to sleep". In the Klingon way of thinking, fire is sort of there all the time, but it's normally sleeping or dormant. Spontaneous combustion would also be described by making use of {vem:v}.[2] There is no one way to say "firefighter". Some options are {qul SuvwI':n} "fire fighter, fire warrior", {qul qaDwI':n} "fire challenger", and (though less frequent) {qul tlhay'moHwI':n} "fire tamer". It's also possible to say {qul QongmoHwI':n} "one who puts fires to sleep", but that's usually not applied until the fire is actually out.[2]
This refers to pieces of animal skin soaked in liquor and set on fire, which must be eaten quickly.
This idiomatic expression literally means "Eat the fire skin!"

definition_fr: son du langage, unité phonétique, phonème
notes: An individual speech sound is {QIch wab:n:nolink}. Speech sounds collectively are {QIch wabmey:n@@QIch wab:n, -mey:n}.

To fully understand the sounds of Klingon, it is recommended that you purchase {The Klingon Dictionary:src}, which has a fuller description of the sounds, as well as the audio recordings {Conversational Klingon:src} and {Power Klingon:src}, in which you can hear them spoken.[1; 2; 3] The transcription system used to write Klingon in the Roman (English) alphabet is phonetic, meaning that words are written exactly as they are pronounced. In the following description of the sounds of Klingon, which is intended only as a rough guide, IPA phonetic symbols are shown between a pair of slashes following the Roman letter or letters used to transcribe each sound. The consonants {b:sen:nolink} /b/, {ch:sen:nolink} /ʧ/, {j:sen:nolink} /d͡ʒ/, {l:sen:nolink} /l/, {m:sen:nolink} /m/, {n:sen:nolink} /n/, {p:sen:nolink} /pʰ/, {t:sen:nolink} /tʰ/, {v:sen:nolink} /v/, {w:sen:nolink} /w/, and {y:sen:nolink} /j/ are pronounced more or less as in American English. {D:sen:nolink} /ɖ/ and {S:sen:nolink} /ʂ/ are retroflex, that is, they are pronounced with the tongue touching the roof of the mouth. {gh:sen:nolink} /ɣ/ is similar to {H:sen:nolink} (see below), but voiced. It sounds somewhat like gargling. {H:sen:nolink} /x/ is like the "ch" in the Scottish word "loch" or the name of the German composer "Bach". {ng:sen:nolink} /ŋ/ is the same sound as is found at the end of the English words "sing" or "thing", but in Klingon it can come at the beginning of words. {q:sen:nolink} /qʰ/ is like the English "k", but with the tongue reaching for or touching the uvula. It sounds a little bit like you're choking. {Q:sen:nolink} /q͡χ/ is similar to a combination of {q:sen:nolink} and {H:sen:nolink}, and sounds like you're really choking and trying to dislodge food stuck in your throat. The Klingon {r:sen:nolink} /r/ is slightly trilled or rolled. {tlh:sen:nolink} /t͡ɬ/ is found in some Native American languages, and is produced by putting your tongue in the position to say {t:sen:nolink}, then forcing air through the sides of your mouth as if to say {l:sen:nolink}. The glottal stop {':sen:nolink} /ʔ/ ({qaghwI':n:nolink}) is a slight pause or catch in the throat, like between the two syllables of "uh-oh". The vowel {a:sen:nolink} /ɑ/ sounds like the "a" in "psalm" or "father". The vowel {e:sen:nolink} /ɛ/ sounds like the "e" in "bed" or "egg". The vowel {I:sen:nolink} /ɪ/ sounds like the "i" in "bit" or "misfit". Note that it is always written as a capital letter. The vowel {o:sen:nolink} /o/ sounds like the "o" in "note" or "mosaic". The vowel {u:sen:nolink} /u/ sounds like the "u" in "prune" or "food". The diphthongs {aw:sen:nolink}, {ew:sen:nolink}, {Iw:sen:nolink}, {ay:sen:nolink}, {ey:sen:nolink}, {Iy:sen:nolink}, {oy:sen:nolink}, and {uy:sen:nolink} are possible, and sound essentially like their components. Note that {ay:sen:nolink} rhymes with English "why" or "my", whereas {ey:sen:nolink} rhymes with "way" or "may". The names of the Klingon consonants consist of the sound followed by {ay:sen:nolink}, and the names of the vowels consist of the sound preceded by {':sen:nolink} and followed by {t:sen:nolink}. The glottal stop is an exception, being called the {qaghwI':n}.[4]

definition_fr: être accompli, être terminé, être réalisé, être atteint, être fini
notes: This verb is used with the suffix {-taH:v} to form {rIntaH:v}, a construction used to indicate finality (cf. the suffix {-ta':v}).[1] By itself, {rIn:v:nolink} is used in radio transmissions to indicate end of transmission, similar to "over".[2]

This special verbal construction follows another verb to indicate that the action described by the preceding verb is a fait accompli. It is similar in meaning to the verb suffix {-ta':v:suff}, but has the additional connotation of finality.

definition_fr: être les pionniers de, percer, innover
notes: This would apply to a scientific breakthrough or discovery, but not to, say, setting a new record in a bat'leth twirling competition.

definition: make a cracking, snapping, or clicking sound; emit a signal (could be sound, radiation, smell, etc.)
definition_fr: émettre un bruit de craquelure, de claquement ou de cliquetis ; émettre un signal (peut être un son, un rayonnement, une odeur, etc.)
notes: This word originally referred only to emitting sound. Later, the meaning was extended to mean emitting any sort of signal: sound, radiation, smell, etc. In comparison, {tlhuD:v} refers only to the emission of radiation.
source: [1] {Saarbrücken qepHom'a' 2017:src}, [2] {DSC - Battle at the Binary Stars:src}, [3] {qep'a' 28 (2021):src}

notes: This is used with {tlhen:v}.[1]
{nIl'atrogh:n}, {ghav:n}
There is no noun in Klingon meaning "color".[1, p.81] This also refers to ink, as for a rubber stamp ({toqwIn:n}).[2]
For example, this is what an ax does to a watermelon.

definition_fr: balise, fanal, phare, feu de signal

notes: Do not confuse this with {ro':n}.
This refers to an imaginary line around which an object spins or is symmetrically arranged.
This can be the object of {naj:v} "dream" or {SIQ:v} "endure" and some other verbs, but generally not {ghaj:v} "have" (unless you somehow literally possess a nightmare).
This refers to a dimension within a coordinate system, not another dimension like in a parallel universe (for which see {'u' quq:n} and {'u' Dop:n}).
Informally, the term {tlhepwI':n} is often used.[1]
See {KGT p.91:src}.
This refers to hair on the face which covers the chin and neck area.[2]
This word is also used by Klingon grammarians to refer to the rule that governs the use of pronominal prefixes, a rule Federation grammarians call "agreement".[2]
This is considered too potent for tourists.
There is an idiom, {matlhHa'; romuluSngan rur}.
This is also called {HoHwI':n} for short.
An item meant for play.[1]
This is the metallic chemical element with the symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
This is an alloy of copper and zinc.

definition_fr: rouler, être en train de rouler
notes: In the context of playing dice, this word refers to the action of the dice as they are rolling. (To "throw" or "roll" the dice would be {ronmoH:v:nolink}.)[1] When applied to a person, it means the person is rolling haphazardly. To perform a somersault is {Hay:v}, and to roll down a hill (like a log) is {tetlh:v}.[2] This verb can be applied to aircraft, for which see {ron:v:2}.

definition: roll (aircraft wings tilt, one up, one down)
definition_fr: rouler (les ailes de l'avion s'inclinent, une vers le haut, l'autre vers le bas)
notes: This is just the verb {ron:v:1} applied to aircraft. For a pilot to roll an aircraft would be {ronmoH:v:nolink}.
This can be used generally, not just for how Terrans tend to ruin food.[1]
Diseases are referred to by the name for the disease followed by {rop:n:nolink}.[2]
This refers to any epidemic, and not specifically the infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis.

definition_fr: Les Klingons ne tombent pas malades.
cicatrice (due à une maladie, une infection, etc.)
notes: This is a scar which is the result of some sort of disease, infection, etc.
This line was spoken in Klingon but was not subtitled.

definition: be fragile, be delicate, be flimsy
definition_fr: être fragile, être délicat, être cassant

notes: This word refers to anyone not a member of the group under discussion. Hence a non-military person in contrast to military personnel, a non-government worker in contrast to government workers, a non-Klingon speaker in contrast to Klingon speakers, etc. This is not used to contrast races, species, nationalities, etc. (For example, it would not be used for a non-Klingon or non-Swede.)[1]

This implies bulk due to body fat or the like, while {pI':v} does not have this connotation. Both can be used to express "not thin", but {ror:v:nolink} is more appropriate to convey "not lean". When this verb is used to describe an inanimate object, there is usually a bit of anthropomorphizing, likening the object to a person or an animal.[2] A "fat book" would be a {paq qargh:n@@paq:n:1, qargh:v}, unless the book comes to life as a character in a cartoon or something like that. (In that case, the plural suffix {-pu':n:suff} might also be expected.)[2]

This is "be fantastic" in the fantasy sense; it does not mean "be wonderful, terrific".[1] The concept of a "fairy tale" might be expressed as {puq lut:n@@puq:n, lut:n} or {lut rorgh:n@@lut:n, rorgh:v} or {puq lut rorgh:n@@puq:n, lut:n, rorgh:v}.[2] This word is also used in mathematics to refer to imaginary numbers ({mI' rorgh:n}).[3]
This is a slang term based on {roS:v:1} or {roS:v:2}, and meaning {qIS:v}.[1]

Chromosomes are numbered (e.g., {roSmaH wej:n:nolink}). The two sex chromosomes are {roSmaH pagh:n:nolink} and {roSmaH bID:n:nolink}. Two {roSmaH bID:n:nolink} chromosomes occur in females, and one of each occur in males.[1]
Do not confuse this with {ro:n}.

search_tags: challenge, put your money where your mouth is
notes: This idiomatic expression is used to challenge someone to take action in a manner consistent with something he or she just said. (It's similar to the English expression "put your money where your mouth is".)

definition_fr: expression idiomatique qui exprime le contraste
notes: This literally means "if the open hand becomes a fist". It is used in a similar fashion to the English expression "on the other hand".
This is the closest Klingon equivalent to the marine crustacean that attaches itself to submerged surfaces.[1]
One of its ingredients is the {DayquS:n} plant.[2]

definition_fr: continuer, procéder, y aller, le faire

notes: Maltz asserts that Klingons never blush.

definition: be physical (subject to laws of physics)
definition_fr: être physique (soumis aux lois de la physique)
notes: This means that something is subject to the laws of physics; it could be applied to something corporeal but also to energy.[1]

This is a noun for a gap in anything that has been torn, like a rip in a shirt (a hole that, if big enough, you can stick your finger through). If you rip something to threads so there are pieces of fabric dangling (not a hole surrounded by otherwise intact fabric), {rulvaH:n:nolink} would probably not apply. If you poke a hole all the way through something (like bread), that's a {rulvaH:n:nolink}. If you break it in half, there's no {rulvaH:n:nolink}.[1]
Don't confuse this word with {ngaj:v}.

The gas produced is called {SIp:n} (a general word for gas of any kind) or {Qep'It:n} (a gas produced within the body).[1] To distinguish between gas emission from different orifices, use a phrase involving {nuj:n}, {Hugh:n}, or {Sa'Hut:n:1}.[2]
This is a city in {ghevchoq Sep:n}.

This refers to controlling or handling something that can or may do something on its own (or due to some source of power), but the manual intervention causes it to do something else or behave differently. It is more likely to be used when the handling alters the configuration of the thing being manipulated, in comparison to {raQ:v:nolink} (which is used if the thing being handled doesn't do anything if it's not being handled). One might {ruQ:v:nolink} a robot vacuum cleaner by picking it up and reorienting it. One would not {ruQ:v:nolink} a {betleH:n} (unless it's an adjustable {betleH:n:nolink} of some sort). If one were to {ruQ:v:nolink} a work of art, that would suggest the artwork is manipulable in some way. Controlling the thrusters by pushing a button or two would be {raQ:v:nolink}, but manually controlling them by physically doing something to them directly, like yanking a thruster component, twisting something, or banging on something, would be {ruQ:v:nolink}.[2]

This verb is used to form similes, such as {puj verengan; bIQ rur@@puj:v, verengan:n, bIQ:n, rur:v} "the Ferengi is as weak as water".[2; 4] It can also be used to translate "like" in the sense of "looks like".[3]
This is a Klingon penal colony, a planet mostly covered in ice. Prisoners are sent to work in its {tlhIlHalmey:n@@tlhIlHal:n, -mey:n}.

definition: He can sell ice on Rura Penthe.
definition_fr: Il peut vendre de la glace sur Rura Penthe.

definition: rhinoceros-like creature, a type of animal
definition_fr: créature ressemblant à un rhinocéros, un type d'animal

notes: This describes a bond such as exists between blood brothers.

definition: be positively charged, have a positive charge
definition_fr: être chargé positivement, être à charge positive, avoir une charge positive

notes: This is a ritual that allows an orphan to join another House.

definition_fr: parfois, quelquefois, de temps en temps
Tout le monde rencontre des tribules de temps en temps.

notes: This refers to part of a computer input device (see {'eQway':n}).

definition_fr: skateboard, planche à roulettes (équipement sportif terrien)

notes: Klingons don't traditionally have a sweet dessert at the end of a meal. This term has been heard for "dessert" in the way Terrans think about it.

definition: be ready to collapse or die (referring to food)
definition_fr: être prêt à s'effondrer ou à mourir (en référence à la nourriture)
notes: This is an upper-class word to describe food that should be eaten live.
This refers to the sound, and not to any letter or glyph.
{jIH:n:1h}:{tlhIH:n} = {Sa-:v:pref,nolink}
The subject is what's undergoing expansion.

definition: be amplified, be fleshed out, be elaborated, be increased in scope, etc.
definition_fr: être amplifié, étoffé, élaboré, élargi, etc.
notes: This is an expansion of the meaning of the existing verb {Sach:v:1}.[1] In the context of zooming (see {jo':v:2}), this can be used for "be magnified".[2]

Another variant of this word which is used with roughly equal frequency is {SanID:n:num,nolink}. This is a number-forming element, and not itself a number. The number 1000 (one thousand) is {wa'SaD:n:num,nolink} in Klingon. Note that Klingon has number-forming elements for "ten thousand" ({netlh:n:num}) and "hundred thousand" ({bIp:n:num}) which are independent of the word for "thousand". While {SaD law':n:nolink} is a grammatical expression, {SaDmey:n:nolink} is not.[3]
To indicate "millennia ago" or "millennia from now", {ret:n} and {pIq:n} are used in place of {poH:n}, respectively.[1]

This is a short-scale billion (i.e., one thousand million).[1] For tens of billions, the number-forming elements {maHSaghan:n:num} or {netlh'uy':n:num} are possible.[2] For hundreds of billions, the number-forming elements {vatlhSaghan:n:num} or {bIp'uy':n:num} are possible.[2] For trillions, the number-forming elements {SaDSaghan:n:num} or {SanIDSaghan:n:num} are possible.[2]

Animals kept as pets by Klingons include the {targh:n}, the {Qogh:n}, and the {'er:n}. Terrans also keep an animal resembling the {vIghro':n} as pets. Commands given to pets should be preceded by the word {SuH:excl}, and always be in clipped Klingon.[2]
Based on its usage in the {paq'batlh:src}, the thing being ascended is the object, and the destination is marked with {-Daq:n}.[2] This word is not used for sort order.[3]
See the example for an illustration of the difference between this word and {nej:v}.
The verb {chenmoH:v} can be used with {San:n}.[2]
This is a scar which is the result of a wound received in the course of a fight or battle.
From lowest to highest, these ranks are: {tay:n:3}, {Sutay:n}, {veStay:n}, {Santay:n:nolink}, {'Iptay:n}.
This refers to an individual plant, typically with stems, leaves, etc. It is not used for fungi or algae.
This is a unit of information in computer science.

definition: land (alight on the ground, like a bird)
definition_fr: atterrir (se poser sur le sol, comme un oiseau)
notes: If a bird lands on a tree, the verb {ngun:v} is used, and if on water, then {tlhot:v}.[2] The landing site (see {SaqDaq:n}) is marked with {-Daq:n:suff}.[4]
This is the native region of {qeylIS'e' lIjlaHbe'bogh vay':n:name} on {Qo'noS:n:place}, and the location of his estate.

Klingons have no tear ducts, and there is no word for tear or tears. However, Klingons eyes do redden ({DoqchoH:v:nolink}) from time to time.[2] They would also understand {mIn 'onroS:n} to refer to a teardrop.
When used adjectivally, this usually follows a plural noun, but it can follow a singular noun if the context is clear.[2; 3]

This means "variety" in the sense of "an interesting variety of tea", not "variety is the spice of life".[2] When the verb {Sar:v} is used adjectivally, it usually follows a plural noun. It can follow a singular noun, but this is unusual and would probably have to be made clear by context.[2] Thus, {tamler Sar:n:nolink} means "isotope" (i.e., a variety of the same element) and not "various elements" (i.e., different elements), which would be {tamlermey Sar:n@@tamler:n, -mey:n, Sar:v}.[3]

definition: sark, type of animal (horse-like Klingon animal)
definition_fr: sark, type d'animal (animal Klingon ressemblant à un cheval)
notes: This animal resembles a horse.

definition: be shallow, be superficial, be uncritical, be unfortunate, be not good
definition_fr: être superficiel, être futile, ne pas être critique, être malheureux, ne pas être bon
notes: This word is applied to a person to disparage his or her intellect. It is also used by itself as an expression of disapproval, similar to {Do'Ha'.:sen}[1, p.164]
This is used for situations like being stuck in a meeting or stuck in traffic. It's also used for a cat stuck in a tree.
A series of usually military operations, either involving a specific type of fighting or terrain, or undertaken to achieve a set goal.[1]
The first and second {yu:n} in the Klingon musical scale are a nonave apart.
{Sawchuq:v@@Saw:v, -chuq:v} would be understood as a same-sex marriage between two men.[2]
To use a gesture is {Sawlay lo':sen@@Sawlay:n, lo':v} or else a specific gesture verb (such as {SIq:v}, {qay:v}, etc.). Maltz didn't know a generic verb for this.[1]

There is some overlap with {ngogh:n}. A {ngogh:n:nolink} has a more-or-less defined shape, whereas a {Sawqe':n:nolink} probably doesn't have a defined or even easily describable one (though it may come close or sort of resemble one). {Sawqe':n:nolink} is generally used for smaller objects, but there is not clear-cut dividing line about size. Certain items tend to always be referred to by one or the other.[1]
This means "surplus" in general, not just in regard to economics.[1]
This is the 2nd rank of {yaS:n:1h}.[2]

This is an extension of {Sa'Hut:n:1} to the back of something, in which case the front would be {logh'ob:n:2} and the sides would be {reD:n:3}.[1] In this usage, the plural is formed with {-mey:n:suff}.[2] This can apply to cars, motorcycles, space ships and the like, but not to the back of a computer screen (too flat) or a bottle (because it's round). There's an overlap with {'o':n}, but whereas {'o':n:nolink} refers to a 3-dimensional space, {Sa'Hut:n:2,nolink} refers to the surface at the back.[3]

This is a large region several thousand kilometers east of the First City ({veng wa'DIch:n}). In the dialect of this region, prepositionals take suffixes (see under {lurgh:n} for an explanation). Furthermore, toasts follow the normal word order, with the subject following the verb (see {-jaj:v}). This region contains {HuD beQ yoS:n}.
This is a ceremonial position whose role is to activate the Beacon of Kahless.

This is for driving things which are self-powered, so it would not be used for a bicycle, for example.[2] It's possible to use this with a motorcycle, but it would be somewhat marked, like saying "drive a motorcycle" in English. (The normal verb to use with motorcycles is {ngIt:v}.)[3]

definition_fr: dispositif de contrôle, appareil de contrôle
notes: Usage of this outside of set, accepted expressions such as {bIQ SeHjan:n} is considered odd.
This can be used for a "settings" or "preferences" page in software, but not individual settings, which are {DuH:n}.[2]
This is the closest Klingon equivalent to a palm tree. For a Terran palm tree, precede this with {tera':n}.[1]
This is the general term for any type of ladder.[1]
Small children, or adults talking to or about small children, use {rIl:v:1} instead.
Small children, or adults talking to or about small children, use {rIlwI':n} instead.
The non-slang way to say this is {nguy:v}.
Identical twins are {SenDeqpu' ghuD:n@@SenDeq:n, -pu':n, ghuD:v}; non-identical twins are {SenDeqpu' tlhIn:n@@SenDeq:n, -pu':n, tlhIn:v}.[1]
There is also a slang term, {ruqwI':n}.
This is the name of a Federation starship (神舟 in Chinese). As this is a non-Klingon name, there is some variation in how Klingons pronounce it. Some pronounce it more like {Senjaw:n:name,nolink}.
Klingons breed some small animals for food.[2]
This is an extension of {Sep:v:1} to mathematics.

This refers to a region whose borders are definable, and which was politically distinct at one time in the past. One appropriate translation for this word might be "country".[2] Some of the known regions of {Qo'noS:n} are: ▶ {ghevchoq Sep:n} ▶ {meqro'vaq Sep:n} ▶ {noHva'Dut Sep:n} ▶ {Qotmagh Sep:n} ▶ {Sa'Qej Sep:n} ▶ {taq'ev Sep:n} ▶ {veng wa'DIch Sep:n} ▶ {voSpegh Sep:n} In {TNK:src}, the category title for "Countries" was translated {Sepmey tlhab:n:nolink} (see {tlhab:v}).[3]
Places with notable regional dialects include: ▶ {meqro'vaq Sep:n} ▶ {noHva'Dut Sep:n} ▶ {Qotmagh Sep:n} ▶ {ruq'e'vet:n} ▶ {Sa'Qej Sep:n} ▶ {taq'ev Sep:n} ▶ {voSpegh Sep:n} ▶ {mo'rISqa':n}
There is an idiom, {let mInDu'Daj; Separmey rur@@let:v, mIn:n, -Du':n, -Daj:n, Separ:n, -mey:n, rur:v}.

definition_fr: être formel, être rituel, être cérémoniel

A signal may be received (or sent) on a particular frequency, expressed in {chaDvay'mey:n@@chaDvay':n, -mey:n}. When a signal is sent out on a number of frequencies simultaneously, it is said to be sent out on {Se'(mey):n:nolink} and not {chaDvay'(mey):n:nolink}, and similarly when monitoring a number of frequencies.[2]
This refers to a device used for two-way communication. For the device which receives (but does not send) an audio signal, see {wab HevwI':n}.
This is a component of a cloaking device.
This is a component of a cloaking device.
This word refers to a publication of any kind, whether printed or not.

The idea of "philosophical people" ({ghotpu' SIb:sen:nolink}) is that they are not professional philosophers (like Plato and Socrates) but rather ordinary people expressing philosophical thoughts in a certain situation.[1; 2]

This refers to the geographic tool, not the drawing tool.

This is the first officer of the {'entepray':n:name} under {jemS tIy qIrq:n:name}.

When used with nouns marked with {-Daq:n}, the finger verbs mean "point (with that finger) at or towards" the object indicated by that noun. There are some special cases of the reflexive (with {-'egh:v}) forms of the finger verbs. See the example below, and also under {rIl:v:1}. If an implement is used for an activity typically performed by a finger, a finger verb may be used.

This is a type of small person in Klingon mythology, like an elf or a gnome.[1] It might be used to translate creatures such as "dwarf" or "fairy" in Terran mythology as well, though it might not be appropriate for translating the term "fairy tale".[2]
This is the scientific term for the pole of a planet. Informally, you can use {'er'In:n} and {megh'an:n} for the two poles of a planet.[1]
Klingons use {SIQ:v:nolink} rather than {tIv:v} for some things that humans might consider pleasant or neutral.
This literally means "string doll", and refers to a doll which is used in puppet theatre performances.
The underlying notion here is one of ridicule or derision. When wanting to be particularly insulting, this might be altered to {SIrHagh:n:nolink}.[1]
This is a value that never changes.[1]
This is the general term like in English "unit of length" or "unit of measure". For example, when a person says "It's five long", someone might reply with "Identify the unit!"[1]
This is an old word. Maltz liked this better than {may' Sut:n:nolink}.
This is what {qorghwI':n} are often made of on Earth.[1]
An artificial waterway or artificially improved river used for travel, shipping, or irrigation.[1]

definition_fr: Que l'esprit de Kahless vive en vous.

notes: This word applies to both food and beverages[2], or anything consumed for sustenance.[4] A single dish or course is called a {nay':n}.[2] This word carries the idiomatic meaning of "matter, concern, affair", for which see {Soj:n:2}.

This is usually served only on the most formal occasions.
The verb to use for compiling such a list is {gher:v}.
This refers to food that no one has done anything to.[1, p.84]
See {KGT p.84:src}.
This refers to any fishlike creature that has to come up to breathe air.[1]

The {Solrogh:n:nolink} is the entire structure, including both railing and support (and other) posts, if any. The word for a vertical post, whether it actually holds up the railing or is there for ornamentation only (or, in mostly non-Klingon sites, safety) is {naSIn:n}. A {naSIn:n:nolink} that actually provides support for the railing is a {Solrogh tut:n@@Solrogh:n, tut:n:1}. The railing alone is a {raqvel:n}.[1]
This is used in the sense of relieving stress or pain. It is not used in the sense of releasing someone from duty.[2]
This is a ceremony which either precedes or is the initial part of the Rite of Succession (see {cho'tay:n:hyp}).

Groups made up of a specific number of members (whether people or otherwise) are referred to idiomatically using this word preceded by the number. {cha' Sonme':n@@cha':n, Sonme':n} could mean twins, but {SenDeqpu':n@@SenDeq:n, -pu':n} is far more common.[1]

definition_fr: salle à manger, salle de repas

notes: Do not confuse this word with {QIch:n}.
Despite its literal meaning, this term can also be used for a music stand.[1]
There is an idiom, {lugh; Sor rur@@lugh:v, Sor:n, rur:v}[2], which may be connected to the verb {Sor:v}. This word can also refer to the "club" suit in a deck of playing cards (see {Degh:n:1}).[3]
This verb is connected with the idiom, {lugh; Sor rur@@lugh:v, Sor:n, rur:v}.
If the context is clear, {Sor Hap:n} or {'awtIr:n} (or even both) may be omitted, but the {-mey:n:suff} cannot be dropped.[1]
One kind of {Sor Hap 'In:n} is a tube which is open on both ends, with a longitudinal slit which doesn't go all the way to either end, and which is struck with a {mupwI'Hom:n}.
This is the metallic chemical element with the symbol Cu and atomic number 29.
The siblings of a {SoS:n:nolink} are {me':n} and {'IrneH:n}.
Known only from {De'wI' SoSbor'a':n}.

definition_fr: être en détresse, être dans la détresse

notes: A slang term is {QIm julHom:n} or even just {julHom:n:nolink}.
This verb can take {'e':n:pro} as its object.[2]
This can mean "awkward" in the sense of "not graceful".[2]
In the {ruq'e'vet:n} dialect, this word is used instead of {ghIH:v:1}.
The subject of this verb hides the object (or hides something in general, if there's no object).[3] This verb is also used for the encryption of data (see {So':v:2}).
This is just an application of {So':v:1} to data.
This is a component of a cloaking device.

definition_fr: moniteur d'émetteur de champ de masquage
notes: This is a component of a cloaking device.
This verb is also used for the decryption of data (see {So'Ha':v:2}).
This is just an application of {So'Ha':v:1} to data. When this term is used for the decryption of data, it implies that the decryption is authorized and the way to do it is known.[1]
Watch Gowron say this: {YouTube video:url:http://youtu.be/BpdgUluBJOQ}

This is a kind of surrogate parent role which is bestowed on a family friend who would care for a child if their parents were incapacitated. The closest analogy for the relation between a soh-chim and a child's parent is a stepbrother or stepsister.[2] This term is gender-neutral and "godparent" is a good approximation. If a gender distinction needs to be made, {loD:n} or {be':n} can be added after {So'chIm:n:nolink}.[3]
{tlhIH:n}:{pagh:n:1h} = {Su-:v:pref,nolink}

definition: be brave, be heroic, be bold, be valiant, be intrepid
definition_fr: être courageux, être héroïque, être audacieux, être vaillant, être intrépide

notes: This can also be used to mean "frequency" in constructions such as {wanI' SubmaH:n} or {yay SubmaH:n}. See {pe''egh:v} for an explanation of how to say something like "4 out of 5 points".
This refers to a dream that occurs when one is sleeping, and not in the sense of a hope, goal, or desire. It is also used to refer to a hallucination.[1]

definition: be green, be blue, be yellow
definition_fr: être vert, être bleu, être jaune
notes: The word {SuDqu':v@@SuD:v:1, -qu':v} would probably be described as "green". {SuD 'ej wov:sen@@SuD:v:1, 'ej:conj, wov:v} refers to a yellowish tinge. ({SuD 'ach wov:sen@@SuD:v:1, 'ach:conj, wov:v} is also heard.)[2]

definition: gamble, take a chance, take a risk
definition_fr: jouer, tenter sa chance, prendre un risque

notes: The literal meaning of this idiomatic expression is "Fek'lhr's eyes are green".

This is also written as {Su':excl:nolink}. Some speakers of Klingon pronounce this word as if it were {SSS:excl:nolink}. This exclamation indicates that the speaker is about to give a command, or is ready to do something or that arrangements have been made for something to happen. ({TKD 5.5:src})

The use of this word involves the concept of deixis. It usually implies the subject is near the speaker, unless the context is set up to indicate the action is taking place somewhere else (for example, using {-Daq:n}). The suffix {-chuq:v} is not used with this verb.[2] The expression {jISum:sen:nolink} has an idiomatic philosophical meaning, "I'm in touch with my inner self" (in a Klingon way).[2]
This refers to how a word would be defined in the same language. See {ghaS:v} for how to express "X means Y".[1]
This word is often the object of the verb {mI':v}. It may be used with or without {-mey:n}. When clearly singular, it refers to a single activity or maneuver.[1]
This is a Klingon plant, parts of which are used to make cloth.
This is a type of {HurDagh:n}. It is smaller than the {leSpal:n} and the {tIngDagh:n}.
See {KGT p.91:src}.

definition: core (e.g., of apple, planet, or star)
definition_fr: noyau (par exemple, de pomme, de planète ou d'étoile)
notes: This might be used for the core of an apple, a planet, or the Sun. But it is not used to refer to the core of a group, which is {qolqoS:n}.
This is a noun referring to the sound (from an animal or otherwise). It is used with {tlhen:v}.[1]
This is a physics term.
A field of physics, like {tujQeD:n} and {tamghayQeD:n}. This is the branch of applied mathematics dealing with motion and forces producing motion.[1]

definition: blow (into wind instrument) to produce sound
definition_fr: souffler (dans un instrument à vent) pour produire du son
notes: This is a general term which is applied to all wind instruments, while {rIl:v:2} is restricted to the {gheb:n}.[2] This can also be used for blowing out a candle ({weQ:n}). Unlike with {jo':v:1,nolink}, air gets out of the thing that's blown onto/into/at (or never goes into it). If {-Daq:n} is used, it implies a miss: air was blown towards the object, but bypassed it.[3]

This is a category of musical instruments with a flexible bag which is alternately filled with and emptied of air. The sound is produced by the air passing over strips of material which vibrate (see {joQ:n:2}). Known types of {SuSDeq:n:nolink} include the {may'ron:n} and the {DIron:n}.
This can be shortened to just {veragh:n} when the context is clear.[1]
From lowest to highest, these ranks are: {tay:n:3}, {Sutay:n:nolink}, {veStay:n}, {Santay:n}, {'Iptay:n}.
The afterlife for the honored dead, where all true warriors go after they die to fight an eternal battle. The closest Klingon equivalent to heaven.

This is someone who does something but does not consider this activity to be their occupation or something done as part of their official duties. There is also a slang term {tavwI':n}. A {Sutlhne':n:nolink} may or may not be {tlhIb:v}.[1]
In ascending order of ferocity, the verbs used to describe military confrontations are: {Qor:v}, {tlhaS:v}, {vay:v}, {lul:v}, {Hargh:v}.

definition: If a warrior does not fight, he does not breathe.
definition_fr: Si un guerrier ne combat pas, il ne respire pas.

notes: This is just the verb {Suv:v} with the suffix {-chu':v}. From the Klingon point of view, to fight perfectly is to fight to the death.[1]

definition: Brute strength is not the most important asset in a fight.
definition_fr: La force brute n’est pas l’atout le plus important dans un combat.

definition: Klingons are born to fight and to conquer.
definition_fr: Les Klingons sont nés pour combattre et conquérir.

notes: This word refers to a specific warrior. For warriorhood as concept, see {vaj:n}.

definition_fr: Il n'y a pas de vieux guerriers.

notes: Sometimes {SuyDar San'on:n@@SuyDar:n, San'on:n} is also used.
Calling someone a {Suy':n:nolink} is considered insulting, comparable to calling someone a "pig" in Federation Standard.[1, p.196]
This is the act of putting one leg or foot in front of the other when walking or running. To indicate the distance covered in a single step, use {Su'Dagh chuq:sen@@Su'Dagh:n, chuq:n}.[1]
This is partially digested and used as a sauce called {quD:n}

This is a general term for any kind of raised profile or relief, such as the ridges on the fingertips, the patterns on a car tire, or the profile of a shoe. It cannot be used for the ridges on the forehead, though. This word is contrasted with {vem:n}, which is the trace left behind when someone touches something. For example, compare {nItlh Su'nIm:n} "fingerprint" (ridges on fingertip) with {nItlh Su'nIm vem:n} "fingerprint" (mark left behind after touching). When used to refer to the fingerprint, etc., as a body part, this word takes the plural suffix {-Du':n}. (Otherwise, it takes the suffix {-mey:n}.) In the following examples, the specific finger or toe name can be used instead of {nItlh:n} and {yaD:n:1}.

This refers to a floor or level in a building, or the level of a platform, and so on. The ground floor is {Su'roq wa'DIch:n}, followed by {Su'roq cha'DIch:n@@Su'roq:n, cha'DIch:n:1,num}, and so on. The basement is {qach DIS:n}.[1]
Generally, {chab:n:1} alone is enough, but a torte could be called this to distinguish it from a cake.[1]
This is a flying insect with largish wings. It originates as a {'ughDuq ghargh:n}.

This is a large whistle with a deep sound, such as on a large seagoing ship (a starship it not likely to have one of these) or at a factory.[1] Such a whistle is not "played" by a person, but powered by an energy source. The verb to activate such a device is {chu':v:2}.[2]
This refers to the sound, and not to any letter or glyph.

This word can be used when talking about phases of a moon, for example, but it's not used to refer to living things (people, animals, plants) except idiomatically. To say to someone {bItab:sen@@bI-:v, tab:v} is to say "you are not applying yourself fully to the task at hand." It would be extremely unlikely to hear a Klingon say {jItab:sen@@jI-:v, tab:v} "I wane" or {matab:sen@@ma-:v, tab:v} "we wane".[1]

This word is not used to refer to living things, except idiomatically. It's not unheard of to say {bItabHa':sen@@bI-:v, tabHa':v} to a lazy worker or trainee who is finally up to speed, but it's not common. But this would never be said to someone who's been training or practicing or working diligently all along.[1]

definition: We will meet in the cocktail lounge.
definition_fr: Nous nous retrouverons au bar à cocktails.

notes: This would be used if something flipped all the way over on its own accord or seemingly on its own accord (even if there is a known cause). If it was flipped over by something else, see {yoymoH:v}. If it was tipped over but not completely flipped, see {qaw':v}. If one flipped over in bed, one would normally say {jItach:sen@@jI-:v, tach:v}. One could say {jItach'eghmoH:sen@@jI-:v, tach:v, -'egh:v, -moH:v} if there were a particular struggle or effort involved. One is more likely to use {tachmoH:v@@tach:v, -moH:v} than {yoymoH:v:nolink} when moving someone from a prone to a supine position (or vice versa). One is more likely to use {yoymoH:v:nolink} than {tachmoH:v:nolink} when flipping hamburgers or pancakes. Either would be fine for flipping over cards, with {yoymoH:v:nolink} implying a quicker or crisper action.

This word also has the idiomatic sense of "don't move!" when given as a command, either as {yItaD:sen@@yI-:v, taD:v} (spoken to one person) or {petaD:sen@@pe-:v, taD:v} (spoken to a group of people).[2; 3] To order someone to literally freeze, the suffixes {-'egh:v} and {-moH:v} would be used: {yItaD'eghmoH:sen@@yI-:v, taD:v, -'egh:v, -moH:v} "Freeze yourself!" ("Cause yourself to be frozen!")[3]
The name of an ice-covered colony planet in the Klingon Empire. Its name literally means "frozen" ({taD:v}).

The subject of this verb is the person or thing starting the process, and the object is the process. For example: {Qu' DataghDI' 'aqtu' mellota' je tIqaw.:sen}[2] If the starter of the process is unknown, unclear, or indefinite, the process becomes the subject of the verb (in which case it takes no object): {taghbej mu'qaD veS.:sen}[3] Instead of using the verb {tagh:v:nolink}, consider using the verb suffix {-choH:v:suff}. For example, a student who is a beginner might be described as a {ghojchoHwI'} (one who is beginning to learn) or said to be {ghojchoH} (beginning to learn).
These are soldiers who fight on foot as opposed to cavalry and other mounted units regardless of external transportation.[1]

This refers to a ship in space which has rotated its nose downwards. A rotation through a negative angle of 90 degrees would mean that the ship's nose was pointed straight down relative to its previous orientation.[2]

Maltz felt sure that there is a connection between this expletive and the expression {bItaHrup'a'?:sen}, but he could not explain what it was.[3]

definition: extra blade on a d'k tahg
definition_fr: lame supplémentaire sur un d'k tahg

notes: Angles are measured in {lawrI':n} (or {law:n} in more ancient times or in traditional documents).[2]
This is the metallic chemical element with the symbol Co and atomic number 27.
This appeared in {STC 104:src} as {DIvI' tamey ngo':n:nolink} "Federation Archives". A single archive record would be {ta ngo':n:nolink}.

For "light" in the sense of "brightness", for example someone's eyes being "sensitive to light", consider {wovtaHghach:n@@wov:v, -taH:v, -ghach:v} instead.[1] A dim light would be {tamghay wovHa':n@@tamghay:n, wov:v, -Ha':v} (whereas {tamghay Hurgh:n@@tamghay:n, Hurgh:v} sounds odd).[2]

Known words for elements include: ▶ {bettI':n} ▶ {bIQSIp:n} ▶ {butnat:n} ▶ {Deltan:n} ▶ {ghav:n} ▶ {jamtlhach:n} ▶ {jelwaS:n} ▶ {jey':n} ▶ {julSIp:n} ▶ {letbIng:n} ▶ {no'negh:n} ▶ {ngIDvoS:n} ▶ {popSop:n} ▶ {qol'om:n} ▶ {reDlIgh:n} ▶ {SIrlIy:n} ▶ {Sorpuq:n} ▶ {tallIt:n} ▶ {targho'nI':n} ▶ {tarngeb:n} ▶ {tI'yap:n} ▶ {velSo':n} ▶ {wa'ngoQ:n} ▶ {voQSIp:n} ▶ {yInSIp:n} ▶ {yuHSIQ:n} ▶ {'apraQ:n} ▶ {'uSqan:n}
Though {vInDa':n} commonly refers to people, in this usage its plural is formed with {-mey:n:suff}. In context, {tamler:n} may be left off.[1]

definition: a bull-like animal, type of animal
definition_fr: un animal ressemblant à un taureau, type d'animal
notes: This word was used in {ghIlghameS:n:nolink}, where {QI'tu' tangqa':n:nolink} refers to the Bull of Heaven.
This is a fruit similar to a cherry. When clarification is needed, for the Earth fruit, precede with {tera':n}.

The residents of this region greatly outnumber the residents of {Qotmagh Sep:n}. This dialect is sort of half-way between the standard dialect and the {Qotmagh Sep:n} dialect. Speakers replace {b:sen:nolink} with {mb:sen:nolink} and {D:sen:nolink} with {ND:sen:nolink}.[1, p.22]
This means "weird" as in bizarre, unnatural, maybe creepy.[2]
This is just a Federation Standard word with Klingon pronunciation.
This is a kind of animal somewhat resembling a dog. It is popular as a pet, but its heart is also considered a delicacy.[2]

entry_name: targhlIj yab tIn law' no'lI' Hoch yabDu' tIn puS!
definition: Your targ has a bigger brain than all your ancestors put together!
definition_fr: Votre targ a un cerveau plus gros que tous vos ancêtres réunis !

notes: This is one of several crab-like animals found on {Qo'noS:n}.
This is the metallic chemical element with the symbol W and atomic number 74. The fact that it seems to contain the word {tar:n} "poison" might just be a coincidence.[1]
This term is used only in reference to food preparation.
This is the metallic chemical element with the symbol U and atomic number 92. The fact that this looks like {tar:n} "poison" and {ngeb:v} "fake" might just be a coincidence.[1]
This verb means to return something somewhere, for example a weapon to the weapons rack. To express the concept of returning to a place, use {chegh:v}.[1]

Though not common, the verb {tatlh:v} can be used with the suffix {-'egh:v} to convey a meaning similar to {chegh:v}. The {tatlh'egh:v:nolink} form seems to suggest that the doer of the action is forcing himself/herself to do something, perhaps because it is difficult or not desirable.
This is what someone might do to wake somebody up, or what one might do to a drink or a limb. What freezing temperatures may do to someone is {jelmoH:v@@jel:v, -moH:v}, not {tav:v:nolink}.
This slang expression literally means "merely shake". If the context is clear that "shake" in the literal sense is not what is meant, {tav:v} alone can be used.[1]
This is a slang term for {Sutlhne':n}, based on the expression {tav neH:sen}.[1]
This is the physical counterpart of a {He:n}, something which one can see and walk on.

definition: Tawi'Yan (the "best man" at a Klingon wedding)
notes: Klingon counterpart (more or less) of the "best man" at a wedding. This is normally translated as "sword-bearer", but etymologically that's not quite right. It's a frozen and somewhat modified form of an old word which was apparently something like {taywI'yan:n:nolink}, having something to do with ceremony or ritual {tay:n:2} and sword {yan:n}, but the details of the old grammatical construction are unknown.[1]
To be even more emphatic, one could say {tawleHnu' pogh:n@@tawleHnu':n, pogh:n}.
This word might be used to refer to a fossil embedded into a stone. It is not used when referring to foreheads.
From lowest to highest, these ranks are: {tay:n:3,nolink}, {Sutay:n}, {veStay:n}, {Santay:n}, {'Iptay:n}.

definition: section of a book or play separate from main portion of the work
definition_fr: section d'un livre ou d'une pièce de théâtre distincte de la partie principale de l'œuvre
notes: This refers to a section of a book or play or the like that is separate from the main portion of the work. It's seldom used without {bI'reS:n} or {bertlham:n}, except when already established by prior context. Despite its description, {taymey:n} is not used for the appendix of a work (for which see {HommaH:n}). A {taymey:n:nolink} contextualizes the main work, whereas an appendix is considered supplemental. This word may be a remnant of the way stories used to be told orally, since they'd begin and end with some sort of ritual ({tay:n:2}), the details of which are lost. Even though {taymey:n:nolink} appears to end with the plural suffix {-mey:n}, it is a frozen form and is considered singular. Thus, it's possible to say {taymeymey:n@@taymey:n, -mey:n} should the need arise.[1]
This word seems to be composed of {tay:n:2} or {tay:v} and {qeq:n} or {qeq:v}. Perhaps this is an indication of what Klingons consider important to a civilisation.
This verb is also used to specify membership in a Klingon House (see explanation under {tuq:n}).
A planet in the Klingon Empire, where the induction into the Order of the Bat'leth takes place.[2]

definition_fr: Le sang et l'eau ne se mélangent pas.

notes: This is short for {ta' tlhIngan Hol:n}.
This is the standard dialect of Klingon. It is also called {ta' Hol:n} for short.
This word is not used to refer to a level in a hierarchy; for that, use {patlh:n:1}.[1]

definition_fr: De grandes actions, de grandes chansons.

notes: The transparent part of the eye that covers the iris and the pupil and allows light to enter the inside.[1]
This verb may be used for filling a hole ({QemjIq:n}), but not for merely stopping up an opening ({qung:n}), which would be {qorgh:v}.[2]
This is a slang usage of {teb:v:1:1}. For non-monetary compensation, see {lev:v:1}.[1]

definition: food server in a Dok'e (fast-food restaurant)
definition_fr: serveur de restauration dans un Dok'e (restaurant fast-food)

notes: Generally, for every {QeD:n} there is a corresponding {tej:n:nolink}.[2]
This is the home planet of a founding member of the United Federation of Planets ({yuQjIjDIvI':n}).
This star system is located near the Federation-Klingon border, and contains the two planets {Doy'yuS:n} and {'elaS:n}.
This means "contradict, disavow, claim as false" and the like. It does not mean "refuse, reject, turn down, don't permit".[2]
This refers to an electronics component.[1]

This is the usual term, but it's actually shortened from {DI'bI'war tem lISwI':n@@DI'bI'war:n, tem lISwI':n}. {DI'bI'war:n} is usually included only in contexts where it is necessary to distinguish a transistor from any device with a similar function but lacking a semiconductor.[1]
This refers to boarding a vessel. It does not take an object.[2]
The child of a {tennuS:n:nolink} is a {tey':n:1}.

definition_fr: oncle (le mari de la sœur du père)

notes: This is used only for numbered pages in a book or something similar.

This is a collection of similar items that are not, or were not originally, attached to each other. With {tlhoQ:n}, the items are typically of different or mixed types. A collection of the same kind of item that are somehow connected to each other is a {yeplar:n}.[1]
In the {BoP:src} poster, this is a type of crane.
For the removal of something from the interior, consider {lel:v}.

definition: assume (surmise or suppose to be true)

The noun formed with {-'a':n:suff,nolink} refers to something that is bigger, more important, or more powerful than the noun without the suffix. Note that the noun with {-'a':n:suff,nolink} need not be better than the bare noun in every possibly way, just in one way that is significant for that noun. For example, a {mIv'a':n} is not necessarily bigger in size than a {mIv:n:1}, and a {toy'wI''a':n} is probably worse off in many ways when compared to a {toy'wI':n}.
The noun formed with {-Hom:n:suff,nolink} refers to something that is smaller, less important, or less powerful than the noun without the suffix.

This is a rarely used suffix, which is used to indicate endearment. It is usually attached to a word for a relative, or sometimes an animal such as a pet. It is suspected that a {qaghwI':n} is inserted before this suffix if the noun ends in a vowel, but no examples are known.

definition: plural (beings capable of using language) (noun type 2)
definition_fr: pluriel (êtres capables d'utiliser un langage) (nom type 2)
notes: This suffix is attached to a noun referring to beings capable of language when there is more than one of that type of being. Note that whether {-pu':n:suff,nolink} is used is a property of the noun, and not necessarily of the things it is referring to. For example, a group of Klingons rendered unable to speak, or a group of Klingon babies too young to understand language, would still be referred to as {tlhInganpu':n:nolink}.[2]

This suffix is used to form the plural of body parts, whether they belong to beings capable of language or to any other animal. However, if a body part becomes separated from a being and is transformed into something which is no longer primarily a body part, then {-mey:n:suff,nolink} is used instead. For example, the plural of {veDDIr:n} "pelt" is {veDDIrmey:n:nolink} rather than {veDDIrDu':n:nolink}.

This is the general suffix for a noun which is neither a being capable of language nor a body part. When this suffix is used for beings capable of using language (instead of {-pu':n:nolink}), it adds the notion of "scattered all about" to the meaning. This suffix cannot be used for body parts (see {-Du':n:nolink}), but this rule is sometimes violated by poets. Some nouns are inherently plural in meaning, with singular forms which are utterly distinct. These inherently plural nouns are treated as grammatically singular, in that singular pronouns and verb prefixes are used for them. When the suffix {-mey:n:nolink} is applied to the singular forms of these nouns, the resulting plural word carries the connotation of "scattered all about".
This suffix indicates the noun is being used in a false or ironic fashion.
This suffix indicates that the speaker thinks the object referred to by the noun is accurately described by it, but has some doubts.
This suffix indicates that the speaker has no doubt that the object referred to by the noun is accurately described by it.
It is considered derogatory to use this suffix on a noun referring to a being capable of language.

This indicates that the noun refers to an object which is nearby or which is the topic of the conversation.[1] For most words designating a fixed period of time, this suffix indicates the current such period: {DISvam:n:nolink} "the current year", {jarvam:n:nolink} "the current month", {Hoghvam:n:nolink} "the current week", etc. However, {jajvam:n} "the current day" is not quite interchangeable with {DaHjaj:n} "today".[2]
This indicates that the noun refers to an object which is not nearby or which is brought up again as the topic of the conversation.

This suffix indicates that an action is occurring (or has occurred or will occur) in the vicinity of the noun to which it is attached.[1] It can typically be used only for physical locations.[2] Some verbs have locative notions in their meanings, and care must be taken when using {-Daq:n:suff,nolink} with such verbs. See {ghoS:v:1} and {jaH:v} for more details. With verbs of shooting, such as {baH:v} and {bach:v}, {-Daq:n:suff,nolink} marks the target. When a verb is used adjectivally, this suffix and the other type 5 noun suffixes are attached to the verb rather than the noun.
This suffix is used when the action is in a direction away from the noun to which it is attached.[1] It can typically be used only for physical locations.[2]
There is a verb suffix {-mo':v} with the same meaning.

This suffix indicates the noun to which it is attached is the beneficiary of the action. It is used to indicate the indirect object when the object is the recipient of the action. ({TKDA 6.8:src}) See {qawmoH:v} for an explanation of how this suffix is used with the verb suffix {-moH:v}.

This suffix emphasizes that the noun to which it is attached the topic of the sentence.[1] It is used with the pronouns to form "to be" constructions.[2] It is also used to disambiguate which noun is the head noun in a relative clause (see {-bogh:v}).[4] If the object noun is marked with {-'e':n:suff,nolink}, it can come before adverbials, which still precede the verb.[3] To use {-'e':n:suff,nolink} on a series of nouns (i.e., nouns joined with one of {je:conj}, {joq:conj}, or {ghap:conj}), it must be attached to each noun individually.[4] This can happen if there are multiple head nouns in a relative clause, or if the subject of a "to be" construction consists of multiple things. In the Morskan dialect (see {mo'rISqa':n}), this suffix is not used to mark the subject in "to be" constructions. If the suffix is used in such a sentence, it serves its usual function of emphasis.[5] Do not confuse this suffix with the pronoun {'e':n:pro}.

This suffix indicates that the subject is unknown, indefinite, or general. It is used only with prefixes which normally indicate a third-person singular object ({vI-:v}, {Da-:v}, {wI-:v}, {bo-:v}, and {lu-:v}; and also {0:v:pref}). This suffix indicates that an action is completed, and the activity was deliberately undertaken. There is a special verbal construction, {rIntaH:v}, which denotes a similar meaning, but has the further connotation of finality.

This suffix indicates that the action is ongoing. When using a pronoun as a "to be" construction to identify the location of something, it's more common to use {-taH:v:nolink} when talking about things which are pretty mobile and leave it off when talking about things which are generally immobile or rarely moved, but this is a tendency only, and not a rule.[3]
This suffix indicates that the action is ongoing, and is proceeding towards a known goal or stopping point.

This suffix is used infrequently by Klingons. It usually expresses extreme politeness or deference, and is normally used only in addressing a superior.[1] This suffix is also used with some verbs of fighting to indicate that the verb refers to a suicide attack. For example, {HIvneS:v} implies that suicide is part of the attack plan, and similarly, {HubneS:v} implies that suicide is part of the defense plan.[2]
This is always used with the type 7 suffix {-taH:v}.
